title: Hall, Yard and Docks
text:
1. Operate within a single enclosed hall whose warehouse floor covers 6,000 m2.
2. Plan all storage, staging and circulation around that footprint without extending activity beyond the marked building envelope.
3. Use the high-bay racking as the primary bulk store, which provides 2,400 pallet positions.
4. Keep racking layouts, clearances and access routes fixed once commissioned, and report any structural change through supervision before moving stock.
5. Serve all inbound and outbound vehicle movements through the building with 8 dock doors.
6. Direct arriving inbound vehicles exclusively to dock doors 1-4 for receiving.
7. Direct loading outbound vehicles exclusively to dock doors 5-8 for dispatch.
8. Recognise that there are 4 outbound dock doors available for scheduling outbound loads.
9. Check the door number displayed above each opening before positioning handling equipment or opening a trailer.
10. Operate each of the 8 dock doors with its own dock leveller.
11. Inspect the leveller, door seal and approach area before starting loading or unloading at any door.
12. Keep main transport aisles clear at all times, noting that main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
13. Allow two-way handling equipment movement in the main aisles only where markings permit, and never store pallets, waste or equipment in that width.
14. Enter rack storage aisles only with suitable equipment, noting that rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
15. Prohibit staging, overtaking or pedestrian loitering inside the narrower storage aisles during handling operations.
16. Separate vehicle routes from the outdoor yard approach to the dock face, and queue trailers only in designated waiting bays.
17. Maintain dock discipline by closing each door and returning its leveller to rest immediately after departure.
18. Keep hall lighting, floor markings and door numbering legible so drivers and floor staff can identify doors 1-4 and doors 5-8 without instruction.
19. Treat the hall, yard approaches and dock face as one controlled system, with capacity governed by floor area, pallet positions and dock availability together.

title: Zones A to F
text:
1. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. All inbound vehicles report to this zone for document checks, unloading and inspection under PR-01 Inbound receiving.
2. Inside Zone A, inbound operators break down loads, verify quantities against delivery documents and segregate damaged or non-conforming goods before any system booking. Cleared pallets move forward only after release from receiving.
3. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. This area provides the main reserve storage for full pallets awaiting replenishment or dispatch.
4. From Zone B, reach trucks place and retrieve pallets in the high bays under PR-02 Put-away to storage and PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Stock remains in its assigned rack location until the warehouse management system directs movement.
5. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Customer orders are picked here against scanner tasks under PR-04 Order picking.
6. Within Zone C, replenishment from bulk storage is completed before the picking shift starts, so pick faces remain stocked throughout order fulfilment. Picked units transfer to packing and then to outbound staging.
7. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Outbound pallets are assembled, wrapped and checked here before loading under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
8. Carriers collect exclusively from Zone D. Dispatchers coordinate door allocation and loading sequence to keep staged freight separated by route and departure time.
9. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Chilled products remain in this temperature-controlled area under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
10. Throughout Zone E, the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and must stay at or below +8 °C. Temperature alarms and shift checks protect this range, and any excursion triggers immediate segregation and review.
11. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Labelling, kitting, rework and other customer-specific tasks take place in this zone alongside controlled storage functions.
12. Returns are inspected in Zone F under PR-07 Returns handling. Delivered returns move directly to the inspection benches, where staff assess condition before any restock, rework or scrap proposal.
13. The quarantine area is in Zone F. Suspect, damaged or pending-decision stock remains physically separated there until inspection, testing or approval releases it.
14. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. Covering 60 m2, the cage provides locked, bunded storage for classified dangerous goods under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
15. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Inbound and outbound movements for the cage are planned to respect this ceiling, with spill equipment and segregation rules maintained at all times.

title: Shifts and Procedures
text: 1. Operate the warehouse on two weekday shifts. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. 2. Plan all inbound, storage, picking and dispatch activity within the assigned shift window. Request additional hours in advance. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. 3. Run every routine task under the controlled procedure system PR-01 to PR-15. Follow the numbered sequence for each goods flow. Do not combine or reorder procedures without instruction. 4. Receive all inbound deliveries under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Complete the required document check, unloading, inspection and system booking in that order. 5. Move booked goods to their storage locations under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Confirm the system booking before any physical put-away. 6. Maintain availability at the pick faces under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Replenish pick faces before the picking shift starts. 7. Pick customer orders under PR-04 Order picking. Work only against scanner tasks in Zone C and scan-verify picked items before packing. 8. Prepare orders for transport under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Verify labelling and wrapping standards before staging. 9. Release outbound loads under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Comply with dock-door assignments and load-release instructions. 10. Process customer returns under PR-07 Returns handling. Inspect returns before any restock, rework or scrap decision. Record the inspection result in the system. 11. Control inventory accuracy under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Carry out daily cycle counts and the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. Post a second count before any stock adjustment. 12. Isolate and report non-conforming stock under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Transfer damaged goods to quarantine and obtain the required approval for any write-off. 13. Operate all handling equipment under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Complete the daily pre-use check before first use each day and wear a seat belt whenever the truck is moving. 14. Protect pedestrians and separate traffic under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Use only segregated walkways and crossings and observe hi-vis and safety-footwear rules on the warehouse floor. 15. Maintain product integrity for temperature-controlled stock under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Respect the cold-zone limits and verify temperature each shift. Handle hazardous materials only under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Observe cage limits and spill-response steps. 16. Respond to alarms and emergencies under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Proceed to the assembly point and complete roll call before anyone re-enters the building. 17. Close each shift in a controlled manner under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Record operating status, open tasks and incidents for the incoming shift.

title: Management and Supervision
text:
1. Accountability for the site rests with a single role. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

2. Within that accountability, operational control is delegated by shift. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.

3. On each shift the chain of command remains explicit. Floor staff report to the shift supervisor on duty for tasking, priorities and immediate decisions.

Across shifts the warehouse manager retains ultimate authority for operations, safety and final sign-offs. No parallel approval route overrides that accountability.

4. Certain decisions are reserved to the warehouse manager and cannot be delegated. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.

Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, stock controllers prepare counts and recounts, but closure requires warehouse-manager sign-off before results become final.

5. Financial authority for loss follows a clear threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

In practice the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Lower-value cases follow the approval route defined in Chapter 2.

6. Working-time authority is similarly reserved. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.

Before any overtime is worked, supervisors submit the request for warehouse-manager approval. Overtime worked without that approval is not authorised.

7. Authorisation to operate handling equipment is a safety-critical sign-off. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

Following training and assessment under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, the warehouse manager grants the individual authorisation. Without it, operation of forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks is prohibited.

8. Incident ownership sits with shift leadership. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report.

Immediately after containment and first response on the shift, the shift supervisor examines the report for completeness, assigns corrective actions and escalates safety matters to the warehouse manager.

9. Coordination between the two levels works as follows:

(a) At shift start, the shift supervisor assumes responsibility for floor staff and incident response;
(b) During the shift, the shift supervisor decides routine operational and safety responses;
(c) Where a matter requires a reserved sign-off, the shift supervisor escalates to the warehouse manager for operations, safety and final sign-offs.

Reserved matters include stocktake sign-off, damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR, overtime approval and authorisation of new forklift operators.

10. Records of all reserved decisions are retained for audit. Sign-offs for stocktake results, write-offs above 500 EUR, overtime and new forklift operator authorisations identify the warehouse manager as approver, while incident reviews identify the reviewing shift supervisor.

title: Operational Roles
text:
1. Inbound operators own the receiving dock operation in Zone A. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.

Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Under PR-01 Inbound receiving they complete the document check before unloading, then unload before inspection, and inspect before system booking. No pallet moves forward to storage until this sequence is complete and the delivery is confirmed in the system.

2. Forklift operators provide all powered transport between zones. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. They execute moves directed by the system or the shift supervisor, including put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage, replenishment under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, and loading support under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Authorisation and daily checks for this group are governed by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

3. Pickers execute customer order fulfilment in the picking zone. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. They work only from replenished pick faces supplied under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, follow the scanner sequence location by location under PR-04 Order picking, and present each picked item for scan verification before it passes to PR-05 Packing and labelling. Pick faces are replenished before the picking shift starts.

4. Stock controllers protect system accuracy across all zones. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Operating under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, they run cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule, lead the second count before any stock adjustment is posted, and prepare results for sign-off. Their adjustments keep put-away, picking and dispatch quantities reliable.

5. Returns staff manage reverse flow inside Zone F. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Working under PR-07 Returns handling, they receive goods accepted within the acceptance window, inspect before any restock, rework or scrap decision, and record condition, quantity and a clear proposal for disposition. Returns are inspected in Zone F and quarantine is also held there when segregation is required.

6. The maintenance technician keeps equipment and infrastructure available. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Duties cover the counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks, pallet jacks, stretch wrappers, dock levellers and racking, with every intervention logged for traceability. Faults affecting safety, cold-chain integrity or dock availability are escalated immediately to the shift supervisor.

7. Dispatchers control outbound flow and carrier access. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, directing inbound arrivals to the receiving side and outbound collections to the dispatch side under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. No trailer is loaded or released without dispatcher confirmation of door, load and documentation, and carriers collect exclusively from the designated dispatch zone.

title: Approvals and Sign-offs
text:
1. Damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR: approval by the shift supervisor is required before disposal, resale or system adjustment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

Within this band the shift supervisor checks the damage report, photographs and quantity, confirms the value calculation, and records the approval in the system. No goods leave the quarantine area in Zone F without that recorded approval.

2. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR: approval by the warehouse manager is required before disposal, resale or system adjustment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

Above the 500 EUR threshold the warehouse manager reviews the same evidence, confirms insurance notification where applicable, and authorises the final write-off value. Floor staff must escalate the case file unchanged when the threshold is exceeded.

3. Stocktake results: sign-off by the warehouse manager only is permitted under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

Following the final recount and reconciliation, stock controllers submit counts, variances and proposed adjustments for review. Without warehouse-manager sign-off, no adjustment is posted to inventory.

4. Inspected returns: final disposition approved by the shift supervisor under PR-07 Returns handling.

After returns staff in Zone F have inspected the goods and proposed restock, rework or scrap, the shift supervisor validates condition, system status and reason code. Restock to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E proceeds only after this disposition is recorded.

5. Overtime: approval by the warehouse manager only is permitted for any additional hours beyond Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

Requests state reason, zone, headcount and duration, and are submitted before the overtime is worked. Unapproved hours are not rostered and are returned for rescheduling within normal shifts.

6. Dock doors and time slots: assignment by the dispatcher governs all arrivals and departures under PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

Carriers receive a confirmed door among dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving or dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch, with a fixed arrival window. Inbound operators and dispatchers work only to the current assignment board.

7. Incident reports: review by the shift supervisor is mandatory for every report.

Immediately after containment and first aid where needed, the shift supervisor examines statements, equipment logs and zone conditions, determines corrective action, and forwards cases requiring site-level decisions to the warehouse manager. Accountability for the whole site, including operations, safety and final sign-offs, remains with the warehouse manager.

8. New forklift operators: authorisation by the warehouse manager only permits operation of forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Authorisation follows valid licence evidence, internal assessment and documented induction. Until the warehouse-manager authorisation is entered on the authorised-operator list, the candidate must not operate any truck unsupervised.

title: Dock Booking and Arrival
text:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving to every inbound delivery from booking through release to inspection.

2. Obtain a booked time slot before dispatching any vehicle to site. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, and no truck may arrive without that confirmation.

3. Direct all inbound trailers to Zone A. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.

4. Use only Dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and must not be used for outbound loading without dispatcher re-assignment.

5. Remember the site context when planning arrivals. The building has 8 dock doors, with the balance reserved for outbound operations.

6. Coordinate all door changes through one owner. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, so contact the dispatcher for any re-booking, delay or door swap.

7. Report to the gatehouse at the booked time with delivery paperwork ready. Wait in the designated holding area until the dispatcher calls the vehicle forward to the allocated door.

8. Reverse onto the allocated leveller bay only when signalled. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller, and inbound drivers must wait for the green light and wheel chocks before opening trailer doors.

9. Secure the vehicle before unloading starts. Apply the parking brake, switch off the engine, hand over the keys where required, and place the trailer under dock control.

10. Keep yard movements under control at all times. Forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, including all manoeuvres around waiting trailers and dock approaches.

11. Slow further on the ramp interface. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches, and forklift operators must sound the horn before entering or exiting a trailer.

12. Leave the door area clear after docking. Instruct drivers to remain in the marked safe area, keep dock levellers engaged during unloading, and notify the dispatcher immediately of any damaged leveller, door or seal.

title: Checking and Inspection
text:
This section implements PR-01 Inbound receiving for document checks, unloading, counting and inspection. Apply it to every inbound delivery without exception. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A under this procedure.

1. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment before entering the floor area. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
2. Verify the vehicle and load against the booking at the dock. Confirm carrier identity, purchase order number, supplier name and booked pallet and carton quantities. Resolve discrepancies with the driver before breaking the seal.
3. Complete the document check before starting any physical unloading. At receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading. Never unload a vehicle with missing or mismatched delivery notes.
4. Unload pallets and cartons to the designated inspection lanes using suitable handling equipment. Inbound receiving requires unloading before inspection. Keep packaging intact during unloading to preserve evidence for damage claims.
5. Count all packages against the delivery note by pallet, carton and handling unit. Use one of the shared handheld WMS scanners to record quantities. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, so return each unit to charge after use.
6. Inspect outer condition, labelling, batch dates and temperature indicators where applicable. Check for crushed corners, wet cartons, broken stretch film, leaking containers and short-dated stock. Photograph visible damage with the pallet label readable.
7. Segregate suspect or damaged goods immediately from clean stock. Place damaged cartons on a separate pallet and attach a hold note. Move temperature-abused or leaking goods clear of other inbound freight pending a decision.
8. Complete inspection before requesting any system booking. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system. Do not pass unchecked goods for put-away.

Under PR-01 Inbound receiving, only inspected and counted goods may proceed to system booking. Against each delivery, record received quantity, damaged quantity, batch and expiry details in the scanner transaction. Attach delivery notes, photographs and damage annotations to the inbound record.

Where shortages, overages or damage are found, notify the shift supervisor on the same shift with quantities and photographs. Hold the affected pallets in the inspection lane until released. Never co-mingle accepted and rejected goods on one pallet.

title: Booking and Release
text:
1. Complete PR-01 Inbound receiving for every delivery in Zone A before creating any system stock record.
2. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.
3. Confirm inspection results for quantity, identity and visible condition are recorded against the inbound delivery.
4. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system (PR-01).
5. Reject any pallet still awaiting inspection from booking; hold it separately until the inspection decision is entered.
6. Book accepted quantities into the warehouse management system under PR-01 Inbound receiving immediately after inspection sign-off.
7. Attach the system-generated pallet licence plate to each booked pallet before it leaves Zone A.
8. Verify on the scanner that destination, batch and quantity match the booking before directing movement.
9. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage (PR-02).
10. Release booked pallets only through PR-02 Put-away to storage; never move unbooked stock to storage locations.
11. Direct ambient reserve pallets to Zone B without delay after release.
12. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
13. Send chilled products requiring controlled storage to Zone E directly after booking.
14. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
15. Route cartons needing additional handling to Zone F in accordance with the inbound instruction.
16. Zone F holds the value-added services area.
17. Record the release time, destination zone and pallet identities in the system as part of PR-02 Put-away to storage.
18. Hand the transport task to the assigned operator only after the booking and release entries are visible in the system.
19. Clear released pallets from Zone A promptly to keep inspection capacity available for the next arrival.
20. Escalate any system booking failure through the defined local process and retain the goods in Zone A until booking succeeds.

title: Storage Limits and Layout
text:
1. Store all ambient reserve pallets in Zone B. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Apply the limits in this section to every put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage.

2. Use only the designated high-bay racking for reserve storage. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Do not place reserve pallets on the floor in front of bays, in cross-aisles, or in any marked pedestrian route.

3. Observe the bay load limit on every level. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Distribute the load evenly across the beams. Never concentrate full-weight pallets on one side of a bay to force fit.

4. Observe the pallet weight limit before assigning a bay. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Check the system weight during PR-02 Put-away to storage. Reject overweight pallets for rework and do not lift them into the high bays.

5. Calculate bay loading on gross weight, not product weight alone. Two full-weight pallets already occupy most of the allowable bay capacity. Verify the combined bay total on the scanner before placing the second or third pallet in the same bay.

6. Keep free block-stacked pallets within both height limits. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Apply whichever limit is reached first. Do not add cartons, drums, or loose layers above the top pallet.

7. Stack only on a level and undamaged base. Align block stacks squarely, with no overhang beyond the pallet edge. Do not stack under damaged sprinklers, leaking roof areas, or leaning rack frames. Keep stacks clear of dock leveller travel paths and emergency exits.

8. Maintain the designed aisle widths at all times. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Do not stage pallets, wrappers, or handling equipment inside these clearances, even temporarily during put-away.

9. Drive and place loads to suit the aisle. Enter rack storage aisles centrally and at low speed. Extend forks only when square to the bay opening. Lower empty forks for travel in main transport aisles. Stop and sound the horn where sight lines are restricted.

10. Keep bays and stacks fit for use. Remove stretch-film tails, broken boards, and loose packing from aisles immediately after handling. Keep beam labels, level signs, and floor markings clean and visible. Leave any bay or block-stack location empty and cordoned off if the structure shows damage until it has been inspected and released.

title: Put-away to Storage
text:
1. Execute all bulk movements under PR-02 Put-away to storage without exception. Confirm system booking is complete before moving any pallet from receiving. Never commence put-away on unbooked stock awaiting release in the system.

2. Direct all ambient reserve pallets to Zone B after release. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Retain allocation discipline so receiving lanes clear promptly for the next inbound trailer.

3. Assign transport work only to qualified operators. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. Select the truck type to suit aisle width, lift height and pallet weight shown on the task.

4. Verify the pallet licence and destination on the scanner before lifting. Scan the pallet label, then scan the target location when prompted. Relocate the pallet solely to the system-directed bay and level.

5. Observe the gross weight limit on every lift. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Reject overweight, collapsed or unevenly loaded pallets and report them for rework before storage.

6. Respect the structural limit of the racking on each placement. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. Calculate the combined weight of pallets already stored plus the incoming pallet before sliding into the bay.

7. Distribute heavy pallets to lower beam levels wherever the system permits. Position the forks centrally, insert fully under the pallet and lower gently onto both support beams. Confirm the pallet sits squarely without overhang.

8. Record each put-away immediately through the scanner confirmation. Against every task, enter bay, level, quantity and any damage observed during transport. Leave the location clean, with stretch film and debris removed.

9. Segregate non-conforming stock during the run and do not store it in Zone B. Hold damaged pallets, incorrect labels or unreadable codes in the designated control area. Notify the supervisor for recount, relabelling or damaged-goods processing.

10. Close the transport task only after the system shows stock in its bulk location. Hand back incomplete tasks with reasons logged for reassignment. Maintain steady flow so booked goods reach Zone B within the same shift.

title: Racking Inspections
text:
1. Inspect every rack bay for structural damage, missing safety pins, deformed beams, loose fixings, overloaded levels and displaced pallets.
2. Verify each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg against bay load notices and system stock records.
3. Check load notices remain legible, correctly fixed at bay ends and match the approved configuration.
4. Examine upright protectors, end frames and floor fixings for impact marks from handling equipment.
5. Confirm pallets sit fully supported on beams with no overhang, collapse or unsafe stacking.
6. Clear debris, stretch film and loose timber from rack bases, beam levels and under-bay areas.

Carry out a documented safety inspection of all racking every month. Record the inspection date, bay range, defects found, load violations identified and corrective actions set. Retain completed records for audit and trend review. Treat the monthly inspection as a standing control alongside daily operational awareness, not as a substitute for immediate reporting.

Report any damaged, suspect or overloaded bay immediately and unload or barrier it until cleared. Prohibit further put-away to an affected bay until the defect is rectified and released. Segregate fallen or unstable stock and prevent pedestrian access beneath the affected level.

Assign detailed examination and rectification to the maintenance technician. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Log every repair with date, bay identifier, fault description, parts used and release signature. Retain impact damage history to target retraining and layout improvements.

Instruct all operators to report rack impacts at once under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Stop the truck safely, secure the area and notify supervision before continuing work. Never straighten, weld, replace or reload damaged components without authorisation.

Review monthly inspection results for repeat damage locations, recurring overloads and overdue repairs. Escalate systemic issues for root-cause action, revised traffic routing or additional protection. Confirm closure of all actions before the next monthly inspection falls due.

title: Cold Zone Handling
text:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every chilled pallet stored in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Do not use any other zone for chilled storage requiring controlled conditions.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Treat +2 °C as the absolute lower control limit for air temperature, product surface temperature where measured, and alarm setpoints.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times. Treat +8 °C as the absolute upper control limit for air temperature, product surface temperature where measured, and alarm setpoints.

4. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. Enter the controlled area at the start of the shift, read the designated display or calibrated thermometer, and record the reading in the temperature log before starting other chilled work.

5. Respond immediately to any reading below +2 °C or above +8 °C. Segregate affected stock in place, prevent further put-away or picking from Zone E, and escalate through the defined cold-chain response path until the temperature returns to +2 to +8 °C.

6. Complete system booking BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Confirm the inbound receipt, batch and quantity in the system, then direct the verified chilled pallet to its assigned location in Zone E without delay.

7. Minimise door-open time and dwell outside Zone E. Stage chilled pallets for immediate movement, close cold-zone doors after each entry or exit, and return temperature-sensitive pallets to +2 to +8 °C storage if handling is interrupted.

8. Document every shift verification, deviation and corrective action under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Record the measured +2 to +8 °C value, the time of the each-shift check, the booked pallet identity moved into Zone E, and the name of the person performing the check.

9. Hand over open temperature issues at shift change. Brief incoming staff on current Zone E readings against the +2 °C minimum and +8 °C maximum, any stock held for temperature review, and any pending re-verification required during the next each-shift check.

10. Audit compliance to PR-12 Cold-chain handling through the temperature logs. Review that Zone E remained within +2 to +8 °C, that manual verification occurred each shift, and that system booking preceded every put-away to storage.

title: Hazmat Cage Limits
text:
1. Store hazardous materials only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F.
2. Keep the cage locked, clearly signed and separated from all other stock in Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.
3. Never exceed 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time.
4. Count every drum, canister, box and pallet toward the limit at gross weight.
5. Check the cage stock balance in the system before accepting any hazmat put-away.
6. Refuse the movement if the additional weight would breach the limit and notify supervision for an alternative instruction.
7. Plan floor use inside the 60 m2 cage to maintain access, segregation and spill containment.
8. Position incompatible classes apart with the required separation distance and keep the containment sump clear.
9. Limit loading to a pallet, including its load, of at most 800 kg.
10. Calculate capacity on that basis: the hazmat cage holds at most 5 full-weight pallets.
11. Stack no pallet above its safe transport height and never block the cage gate, extinguishers or spill kit.
12. Wear a high-visibility vest and safety footwear class S3 whenever entering the cage or handling hazmat on the warehouse floor.
13. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for receipt, storage, separation, labelling and spill response.
14. Inspect packages for leakage, damage and correct labels before placing them in the cage.
15. Isolate leaking or damaged units immediately, contain the spill and report the event under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
16. Record every receipt, issue and relocation by quantity, weight and location on the same shift.
17. Verify the cage total daily and reconcile any difference before further put-away.
18. Prohibit ignition sources, decanting and repacking inside the cage unless PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response expressly permits the task.
19. Keep safety data sheets, segregation chart and emergency contacts posted at the cage entrance.
20. Maintain clear aisles around the cage for inspection, firefighting access and emergency removal of stock.

The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and forms a dedicated 60 m2 compound. Its limit protects containment capacity, separation distances and emergency access. Exceeding 4,000 kg removes that protection and is therefore prohibited.

Treat the 5-pallet equivalent as a planning aid only. The binding control remains 4,000 kg gross. Lighter pallets may increase the pallet count without breaching the weight limit, provided segregation, stability and access remain fully maintained.

title: Replenishment of Pick Faces
text:
1. Execute PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces to feed Zone C before any order picking begins.
2. Confirm all replenishment tasks in the warehouse system and work strictly in task sequence.
3. Draw reserve stock exclusively from Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking.
4. Deliver reserve stock directly to Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
5. Under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts.
6. Assign all pallet movements between Zone B and Zone C to forklift operators.
7. Operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks only within training and authorisation.
8. Retrieve the directed pallet from its bulk location and check label, product and quantity against the task.
9. Transport the pallet to the assigned pick face in Zone C without intermediate staging.
10. Undertake replenishment of full pallets and topping-up of flow racks as separate task types.
11. Place full replacement pallets into the ground-level pick position with the label facing the aisle.
12. Decant topping-up quantities onto the flow rack lanes by product and batch, preserving stock rotation.
13. Return any part-pallet remainder to its defined bulk location in Zone B immediately after decanting.
14. Scan every source and destination location to confirm completion of the movement in the system.
15. Report empty bulk locations, damaged pallets or short reserve quantities during replenishment without delay.
16. Keep replenished pick faces clean, aligned and fully accessible for the incoming picking shift.
17. Within Zone C, separate replenishment activity from early picking activity by lane and by task status.
18. Leave no replenishment equipment, wrapping material or empty pallets blocking ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
19. Close all PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces tasks in the system before releasing Zone C for picking.
20. Escalate any incomplete replenishment to supervision so picking does not start on an unfilled face.

Forklift operators carry out the physical transfer from high-bay racking to the picking zone. Coordination under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces ensures Zone B supplies Zone C in time.

Because pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts, availability at shift start depends entirely on disciplined completion of replenishment. No picking task may draw from a face flagged as awaiting replenishment.

Accuracy in Zone B retrieval determines accuracy in Zone C picking. Label control, batch discipline and system confirmation link bulk storage to the ground-level pick faces and flow racks without interruption.

title: Scanner Order Picking
text:
1. Execute PR-04 Order picking only in Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Accept no picking task outside the assigned faces.

2. Report to the designated pick start point with high-visibility vest fastened and safety footwear class S3 worn correctly. Enter the warehouse floor only when both items are in place.

3. Draw a handheld WMS scanner at shift start and confirm log-on under your own user identity. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, so return the unit promptly for the next user.

4. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks. Follow the scanner sequence screen by screen and never select locations manually.

5. Scan the location label first, then scan each item or carton as directed by the task. Place the quantity confirmed by the scanner directly into the order tote or onto the assigned pallet.

6. Verify quantity discrepancies immediately through the scanner exception function. Leave the stock in the pick face and await system instruction before continuing.

7. Keep totes, cartons and pallet jacks clear of adjacent pick faces while working. Maintain access for other pickers moving along the same flow racks.

8. Handle product labels, barcodes and packaging without obscuring or damaging them during the pick. Position every picked unit so its barcode remains scannable downstream.

9. Close each scanner task only after the system confirms completion of all lines. Check the device display for the task-complete message before starting the next order.

10. Transfer completed totes and pallets to the defined collection point for packing without delay. Ensure picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling.

11. Report damaged stock, short pick faces or unreadable barcodes to the replenishment team through the scanner. Do not substitute alternative locations unless instructed by the system.

12. Return the handheld WMS scanner to the charging rack at task end or shift end. Log off the device and confirm the returned unit shows charging status.

13. Wear high-visibility vests throughout all movements on the warehouse floor, including travel between pick faces and the collection point. Keep safety footwear class S3 laced and in serviceable condition during the entire picking assignment.

14. Work exclusively from live scanner tasks in Zone C. Never pick from memory, paper notes or verbal instruction, and never advance orders that the system has not released.

title: Transfer to Dispatch
text:
1. Complete every PR-04 Order picking scanner task inside Zone C before moving any tote, carton or pallet toward packing.
2. Verify each picked item against its scanner task while still at the ground-level pick faces and flow racks of Zone C.
3. Hold any short, damaged or unreadable item at the pick face and report it through the scanner before continuing the transfer.
4. Undertake scan verification of picked items BEFORE packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling without exception.
5. Present only scan-verified picks for PR-05 Packing and labelling; never forward unverified or partly verified picks.
6. Affix the carton or tote label immediately after successful verification to preserve identity through the handover.

Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. All picks originate there and retain their task reference until packing accepts them. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. All packed orders move there for outbound staging.

7. Transport verified totes and cartons from Zone C to the packing workstations using the designated pedestrian-separated routes.
8. Stage packed cartons by outbound load or carrier route to prevent mixing of orders destined for different trailers.
9. Keep fragile, heavy and part-pallet consignments separated during movement so packing can wrap and stack them correctly.
10. Segregate chilled picks requiring controlled storage from ambient picks during transfer and identify them clearly for priority packing.
11. Inform packing staff of any replenishment delay, substitution or short quantity that affects the completeness of the delivered picks.
12. Return empty totes, spare cartons and unused labels to their defined points before starting the next Zone C collection.

Packing and onward staging depend on a clean handover. Picks without scanner confirmation disrupt PR-05 Packing and labelling and delay release to Zone D.

13. Operate electric pallet jacks for bulk transfer of completed picks where volume requires it and walk the load to packing.
14. Maintain pick sequence and load orientation during travel to allow immediate scan-verification at packing without re-sorting.
15. Direct completed packing output promptly to Zone D for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
16. Confirm the staging location in Zone D with the dispatcher before depositing packed pallets or cages.
17. Position transferred stock within the marked outbound staging lanes and keep access to docks 5-8 unobstructed at all times.
18. Release the transfer in the system immediately after physical deposit so packing and dispatch records remain aligned.
19. Record any damage, spillage or label loss observed during movement and escalate it to the shift supervisor on the same shift.
20. Leave Zone D staging areas clean, with stretch film, strapping and waste returned to their points after each transfer run.
21. Close the PR-04 Order picking task only after the system confirms successful handover of all lines to packing or Zone D staging.

title: Packing and Wrapping
text:
1. Execute PR-05 Packing and labelling for every outbound order before transfer to staging. Complete scan verification, packing, labelling and wrapping in that sequence without omission.

2. Scan-verify picked items BEFORE packing. Scan each item or carton against the order task and wait for system acceptance. Do not place any unverified item into a carton, tote or onto an outbound pallet.

3. Segregate shortages, damages and unreadable barcodes at the pack bench. Do not substitute products. Do not pack damaged goods. Escalate the exception through the scanner and continue with the next verified line.

4. Select the correct carton, tote or pallet for the order profile. Keep consignments clean, dry and stable. Align cartons squarely on the pallet without overhang. Maintain readability of all product and handling labels during assembly.

5. Affix the carton or tote label immediately after successful scan verification. Confirm consignee, order reference and quantity on the label match the system task. Reprint distorted or illegible labels before sealing the carton.

6. Weigh or check the built pallet against the weight limit during packing. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Split overweight builds onto a second pallet. Never dispatch an overweight pallet to staging.

7. Wrap every outbound pallet on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Queue pallets at the wrappers to maintain flow and report any wrapper fault without delay.

8. Verify wrapping coverage before staging. Check that film secures all layers to the pallet base, corners are protected and the top label remains scannable. Re-wrap loose, torn or uneven loads. Verify labelling and wrapping before staging for transfer.

9. Flatten all empty cartons and feed cardboard waste to the site baler. The site has 1 cardboard baler. Keep the packing area clear of loose strapping, film tails and collapsed boxes. Do not leave waste on pack benches or in the transfer lanes.

10. Direct completed packing output to Zone D for outbound staging. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Confirm the staging location before moving packed pallets or cages from the packing area.

11. Stage packed pallets by load, route and door sequence. Keep consignments for different trailers separated and clearly labelled. Do not block dock approaches, levellers or emergency routes with staged pallets.

12. Close PR-05 Packing and labelling tasks only after packing, labelling and wrapping are complete and the system shows the correct packed quantity. Hand over staged pallets for dispatch loading with complete documentation attached.

title: Staging and Loading
text:
1. Execute PR-06 Outbound dispatch for every released load from staging through sealing. Stage only released and wrapped pallets. Check the release in the system before moving any pallet to the outbound area.

2. Direct all outbound staging to Zone D in front of docks 5-8. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Keep staged pallets clear of levellers, roller doors and vehicle swept paths until loading starts.

3. Obtain the door and time slot from the dispatcher before staging. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not move loads to a door without a dispatcher assignment.

4. Use only dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Position the staged load by door number, destination and trailer, and keep door 5, 6, 7 and 8 lanes separately marked and readable from the forklift seat.

5. Verify each pallet before staging. Confirm wrapping is intact, the label is readable and the pallet, including its load, does not exceed 800 kg. Reject overweight, unstable or unwrapped pallets for rework and do not load them.

6. Operate one dock leveller per door during loading. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Inspect the leveller, dock seal and vehicle bed before placing the first pallet. Confirm the trailer is braked, chocked and flush to the dock.

7. Drive at walking pace on all dock interfaces. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Square up to the leveller, cross centrally without turning, and stop before raising or lowering forks inside the trailer.

8. Load in reverse order of delivery, distributing weight evenly over the trailer bed. Count every pallet onto the trailer against the load list. Secure gaps with approved dunnage and re-wrap any pallet damaged during handling before it is stowed.

9. Escalate maintenance faults affecting safety, cold-chain integrity or dock availability immediately to the shift supervisor. Include leveller defects, damaged dock doors 5-8, failed seals and blocked approaches. Do not continue loading on a defective door until released back to use.

10. Seal the trailer only after the load count matches the released quantity. Record the seal number against the load in the system, photograph the sealed doors where required, and hand the documents to the driver. Release the vehicle from Zone D without delay to keep the next slot free.

title: Load and Capacity Rules
text:
1. Apply all trailer, van and shift limits under PR-06 Outbound dispatch before confirming any loading plan.
2. Treat 800 kg as the maximum gross weight for a pallet, including its load, for every capacity calculation.
3. Plan contracted curtain-side trailers on a payload of 22000 kg.
4. Plan the same trailers on 33 floor pallet positions.

Weight therefore governs full-weight loads before floor space is exhausted. Divide the payload by the maximum pallet weight and cap the result by the available floor positions for each vehicle type.

5. Load a trailer with at most 27 full-weight pallets.
6. Reject any plan that places 28 full-weight pallets on one trailer, even where empty floor positions remain visible.
7. Distribute lighter pallets by both weight and footprint. Count the total kilograms against 22000 kg first, then count occupied positions against 33 pallets before releasing the load.
8. Plan the delivery van on a payload of 1200 kg.
9. Plan the same van on 6 pallet positions.
10. Load the van with at most 1 full-weight pallets.
11. Transfer any order exceeding the van weight limit to a trailer. Never split a 800 kg pallet to meet the van payload.
12. Combine up to 6 lighter pallets in the van only where their combined gross weight remains within 1200 kg and each pallet sits on its own floor position.

Shift throughput follows directly from door availability and turnaround. Use the fixed door count and the fixed loads per door to cap bookings for each shift.

13. Operate with 4 outbound dock doors.
14. Handle 3 trailer loads per shift through each outbound door.
15. Cap outbound throughput at 324 full-weight pallets per shift.
16. Derive the shift cap as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer. Stop accepting additional full-weight pallets for the shift once the calculation reaches 324 full-weight pallets per shift.
17. Sequence trailer arrivals to protect the 3 loads per door rhythm. Hold late vehicles off the leveller rather than double-stacking pallets at the dock edge.
18. Record planned pallet count and planned gross weight on every load sheet. Compare both figures against 27 full-weight pallets for trailers and 1 full-weight pallets for the van before authorising loading.
19. Escalate any request to exceed trailer, van or shift limits through the defined release control. Move no extra pallet until a revised PR-06 Outbound dispatch plan confirms weight, positions and door capacity remain compliant.

title: Daily Cycle Counts
text:
1. Execute PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule.
Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, and therefore plan, supervise and close each daily count.
Across the working week rotate through all storage areas so that bulk locations, pick faces and special storage receive repeated verification without interrupting outbound flow.

2. Generate the count list in the warehouse management system at the start of the shift.
Select the scheduled zone for the day and lock the proposed locations before counters enter the aisles.
During picking or replenishment activity, coordinate timing with the shift supervisor so open pallets are counted between movements rather than during them.

3. Assign trained counters and equip each one with a handheld WMS scanner.
Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, so draw the required units from the common pool and return them promptly at task end.
Verify scanner login, zone filter and battery level before leaving the charging rack.

4. Count from the physical stock to the system, not from the system to the shelf.
Scan every pallet licence plate and location label in the assigned sequence, entering quantity, batch and condition exactly as found.
Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, never adjust a quantity during the first pass, even when an obvious difference appears.

5. Compare the first count to system stock immediately after submission.
Where quantity, batch or location differs, order a second count by a different person, using a separate scanner session.
A second count happens BEFORE any stock adjustment is posted, without exception.

6. Investigate the cause when the second count confirms a variance.
Check for open replenishment tasks, delayed put-away bookings, mis-scanned picks and misplaced pallets in adjacent bays before proposing an adjustment.
Stock controllers review the evidence, approve the recount record and post only the verified correction in the system.

7. Close the daily cycle and preserve full traceability.
Confirm that all generated count tasks show complete, all recounts show resolved and all adjustments show posted with reason codes.
Hand any unresolved differences, damaged labels or unreadable barcodes to the replenishment team and to the next shift through PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
Archive the count sheets and scanner logs in the system for audit, and release the counted zone for normal picking, put-away and dispatch.

title: Annual Stocktake
text:
1. Execute PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts as the controlling instruction for this wall-to-wall count. Follow its task sequence without omission, and record every count directly in the system.

2. Plan one full wall-to-wall stocktake once a year to verify all storage locations in a single event. Schedule the freeze of inbound, outbound and internal movements around the count window.

3. Assign stock controllers to own inventory accuracy throughout preparation, counting, recounts and adjustments. Direct all count teams to take tasks from them and return results to them for review.

4. Brief every counter on scanning discipline, location discipline and exception tagging before entering the aisles. Issue the count sheets or scanner sessions by location and retain the issue log for audit.

5. Freeze the assigned locations for the duration of the count. Prohibit put-away, replenishment, picking and transfers into or out of a frozen location until its count is released.

6. Count every pallet, carton, tote and part-pallet in its home location. Scan each location label and each licence plate or item barcode exactly as instructed in PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.

7. Treat any unreadable label, damaged packaging or unbooked stock as an exception. Leave the stock in place, flag the location clearly, and record the exception in the scanner for later resolution.

8. Compare the first count against system stock immediately after capture. Order a second count for every location with a difference before any stock adjustment is posted.

9. Ensure a recount happens before any adjustment under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Prohibit posting, correcting or forcing the system quantity until the second count result is entered and reviewed.

10. Consolidate all first counts, second counts and open exceptions into a single result pack. Place responsibility for completeness and inventory accuracy of that pack with the stock controllers.

11. Present the result pack for final sign-off to the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Allow no other role to close the annual event.

12. Apply the rule that only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. Withhold adjustment posting, financial reporting and release of the freeze until that signature is recorded.

13. Post approved adjustments strictly as signed off, location by location. Verify that system stock equals verified physical stock before reopening each area to normal operations.

title: Recounts and Adjustments
text:
1. Apply PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts to every recount and every inventory adjustment without exception.
Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
Coordinate all second counts through the assigned stock controller on duty.

2. Initiate a recount whenever the first count differs from the system quantity.
Record the original count quantity, location and time before requesting verification.
Retain system stock unchanged while the difference remains unresolved.

3. Assign the recount independently from the first count.
Provide the recount operator with location and product identification only.
Withhold the first count result to avoid influencing the second count.

4. Execute the recount by full physical verification of each affected location.
Scan every pallet licence plate, carton and item present at the location.
Count opened cartons by single units and sealed cartons by stated quantity after visual check.

5. Compare both counts immediately after the recount is entered.
Where both physical counts agree with each other but differ from the system, prepare an adjustment proposal.
Where the two physical counts disagree, order a further verification before any proposal proceeds.
Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, a second count happens BEFORE any stock adjustment is posted.
Never post an adjustment on the basis of a single count alone.

6. Document each adjustment proposal with location, product code, batch, system quantity, verified quantity and both count records.
Attach scanner logs and notes on damaged packaging, misplaced stock or labelling errors where observed.
Submit the completed proposal package to the stock controller for review.

7. Obtain final authorisation before posting to the system.
Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.
Post the approved adjustment in the system without delay.
Brief pickers, replenishment staff and inbound operators on corrected quantities affecting open tasks.

8. Close the case only after the system reflects the verified stock.
File both count sheets, the approved proposal and the posting confirmation together.
Monitor the location during the next working cycle for repeated deviation.

title: Returns Inspection
text:
Execute PR-07 Returns handling for every customer return arriving at the warehouse. Accept only goods returned within 14 days of delivery. Reject consignments outside the acceptance window through the standard refusal routine.

1. Direct all return deliveries to Zone F for inspection. Do not unload returns in any other zone.
2. Confirm the delivery reference, customer identity and original delivery date at receipt. Record the return reason exactly as declared by the carrier or customer documentation.
3. Verify the elapsed time since delivery before opening any carton. Quarantine late returns separately and escalate them for a documented exception decision.
4. Assign each accepted return to returns staff without delay. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
5. Open every carton, tote and item package in the value-added services area. Zone F holds the value-added services area and provides the controlled inspection benches, lighting and system access for PR-07 Returns handling.
6. Inspect every unit for completeness, condition, labelling and resale suitability. Check quantities against the return note, test functionality where the product type requires it, and photograph visible damage.
7. Segregate inspected units by proposed outcome immediately after inspection. Keep restock candidates clean and protected, place rework candidates in the marked rework flow, and isolate scrap candidates to prevent mixing.
8. Record inspection findings, quantities and the proposed restock, rework or scrap outcome in the system on the same handling. Attach photographs and shortage or damage notes to the return record.
9. Present every inspected return for a disposition decision. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision.
10. Obtain approval from the shift supervisor for the final disposition of inspected returns. Do not restock, rework or scrap any unit without that approval.
11. Label approved restock units with the system-generated identification and route them to the assigned storage or pick location. Transfer approved rework units to the defined rework flow inside Zone F.
12. Move approved scrap units to the designated scrap hold and post the system movement promptly. Retain the inspection record, disposition approval and quantity evidence with the return file for audit.
13. Clear inspection benches after each return and return scanners, tools and packaging materials to their defined places. Hand over incomplete inspections with quantities and status notes at shift change.

title: Disposition Decisions
text:
1. Execute all disposition decisions strictly under PR-07 Returns handling and never decide restock, rework or scrap without a completed inspection.
2. Inspect every return in Zone F before proposing any onward route, since returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision.
3. Assign the inspection and proposal task to returns staff, who inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
4. Record the inspection result on the scanner or returns form immediately, including identity, quantity, batch where applicable, visible damage and reason for return.
5. Propose restock only for saleable goods in original resale condition with intact packaging, correct labels and readable barcodes.
6. Direct approved restock pallets and cartons to Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, through the normal booking and put-away flow.
7. Propose rework for goods that remain usable after cleaning, relabelling, repacking or minor repair, and segregate them clearly from saleable stock.
8. Propose scrap for goods that are damaged beyond repair, contaminated, expired or unsafe for resale or rework.
9. Within Zone F, retain goods awaiting a decision in the quarantine area, which is located in Zone F, fully separated from bulk and pick stock.
10. Label each pallet, cage or carton in quarantine with return reference, date, proposer name and proposed disposition to prevent premature movement.
11. Obtain approval from the shift supervisor for the final disposition of every inspected return before any physical move or system transaction.
12. Under PR-07 Returns handling, the shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns, and that approval authorises restock, rework or scrap.
13. Never override a rejected proposal without a fresh inspection and a new approval from the shift supervisor.
14. After approval, release restock quantities for put-away to Zone B without delay and update the system to reflect available stock.
15. After approval, transfer rework quantities to the designated rework holding point and update the system to show blocked or work-in-progress status as applicable.
16. After approval, transfer scrap quantities to the designated scrap holding point and process them under the damaged-goods controls.
17. Close the PR-07 Returns handling task only after inspection, proposal, shift supervisor approval and physical transfer are all recorded, ensuring complete traceability from receipt to restock, rework or scrap.

title: Quarantine and Write-offs
text:
1. Apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling to every pallet, carton and item found damaged, leaking, crushed or otherwise unfit for normal stock.

2. Move the affected goods to quarantine without delay. Segregate the damaged quantity from saleable stock at the point of discovery and transfer it under control to the quarantine area.

3. Retain all goods awaiting a damaged-goods decision in the quarantine area in Zone F. Do not return quarantined goods to bulk, pick faces or dispatch until PR-09 Damaged-goods handling releases them.

4. Note that Zone F holds the value-added services area. Keep quarantine segregated from inspection, rework and labelling work within that area so quarantined goods cannot be mixed with goods under rework.

5. Record the damage at quarantine receipt. Enter the product identity, quantity, location of discovery, nature of damage and photographic evidence where the procedure requires it, and link the record to the original inbound, storage, picking or returns task.

6. Protect the quarantined goods while they are held. Stack them stably, keep access routes clear, prevent further damage and isolate any goods that present a leakage or contamination risk until assessed.

7. Propose restock, rework or scrap for each quarantined line in accordance with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Submit the proposal with the supporting evidence and quantity for approval before any disposal, rework instruction or system adjustment.

8. Obtain approval for every write-off before posting it. Present the value of the damaged goods and the proposed scrap quantity to the authorised approver and record the decision.

9. Escalate write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager. Do not scrap, dispose of or adjust goods above that value without that approval.

10. Request approval from the shift supervisor for write-offs up to 500 EUR. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and decides these lower-value cases during the shift.

11. Refer write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for final decision. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and provides the final sign-off on higher-value losses.

12. Execute only the approved disposition. Complete rework through the defined route, return approved restock to stock through the system, or scrap approved goods securely and post the write-off after the required approval is recorded.

13. Close the quarantine record after physical completion. Confirm that the approved quantity has been reworked, restocked or scrapped, that the system reflects the outcome, and that no residual quantity remains in the quarantine area in Zone F.

14. Review quarantine holdings each shift. Chase overdue proposals, overdue approvals and overdue disposals, and keep the quarantine area clear for new arrivals requiring assessment under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

title: Fleet and Authorisation
text:
1. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation to every movement of powered and manual handling equipment on site.
2. Restrict operation of forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks to designated forklift operators.
3. Within that scope, forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks as directed by task assignment.
4. Maintain the authorised fleet at the established composition without substitution or addition.
5. Deploy 6 electric counterbalance forklifts for general yard, dock and bulk transport duties.
6. Observe that counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t and never exceed that rated capacity during lifting or travel.
7. Assign the 4 reach trucks for the high bays to high-level racking work in narrow storage aisles.
8. Respect that reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t and select attachments and loads accordingly.
9. Utilise the 8 electric pallet jacks for horizontal pallet transfer, replenishment support and dock work.
10. Keep the 12 hand pallet jacks available for short-distance manoeuvring and backup where powered units are unsuitable.
11. Segregate electric charging and parking positions from pedestrian routes and keep access to equipment unobstructed.
12. Obtain warehouse manager authorisation before any new forklift operator is permitted to operate independently.
13. Because only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators, withhold keys and task assignments until written authorisation is confirmed.
14. Verify existing licences, site induction and practical competence during the authorisation review.
15. Record each authorisation in the operator register with date, equipment types and scope of permission.
16. Withdraw authorisation promptly following unsafe behaviour, failed reassessment or loss of qualification.
17. Direct newly authorised operators to work initially under close oversight until consistent compliance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation is demonstrated.
18. Report any defect, damage or missing safety device on counterbalance trucks, reach trucks, electric pallet jacks or hand pallet jacks through the defined maintenance channel.
19. Remove faulty equipment from service immediately and prevent reuse until repair and release are documented.
20. Audit fleet numbers, capacities and authorisations routinely to ensure 6 electric counterbalance forklifts at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks remain available with only warehouse manager approved operators in control.

title: Daily Checks and Maintenance
text:
1. Complete the documented pre-use check under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for every truck assigned to the shift.

Under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation the daily forklift check happens before first use each day. Never start a travel or lift movement until the check for that truck is finished and recorded.

2. Carry out the check on the actual truck to be driven, not on a similar unit parked nearby.

Walk around the truck for visible damage, leaks, tyre condition and fork condition. Test service brake, parking brake, steering response, horn, lights, reversing alarm and emergency stop where fitted.

3. Inspect load-handling and energy systems with the truck stationary and secured.

Verify chains, hoses, guards and backrest for wear or obstruction. Confirm battery charge, cable seating, hydraulic oil indication and overhead guard fastenings show no defect preventing safe operation.

4. Record every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day in the designated log.

Enter truck identity, date, checker name, result and any defect code. Sign the entry immediately after the examination so the record links one check to one truck and one operator.

5. Quarantine any truck that fails the pre-use examination.

Attach the defect tag, remove the keys, park the unit in the marked faulty-equipment position and notify supervision through the standard fault channel. Do not attempt a temporary repair on the shop floor.

6. Hand all defects and damage reports to the maintenance technician without delay.

The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Provide the truck identity, fault description, check sheet reference and location to allow prompt assessment and prioritisation.

7. Obtain maintenance release before returning a repaired truck to service.

Confirm the repair entry is closed in the maintenance log with date, action taken and parts used. Retain the release note with the daily check records for audit and trend review.

8. Review open MHE faults at shift handover and confirm follow-up ownership.

Carry forward any truck still awaiting parts or external service. Brief incoming operators on substitutions issued and on any operating restriction imposed pending full repair.

9. Monitor repetitive defects across the fleet and escalate the pattern.

Where daily sheets show repeated brake fade, steering play, hydraulic seepage or electrical faults on the same truck, request a deeper inspection. Retain completed check sheets and repair logs as evidence for the maintenance plan.

10. Keep check and maintenance documentation complete, legible and retrievable.

File daily sheets by date and truck, cross-referenced to the corresponding repair log entries. Make the file available for safety inspections, incident investigation and management review of PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation compliance.

title: Safe Driving Rules
text:
1. Operate all trucks strictly under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on every shared route.
2. Inside the building, drive forklifts at no more than 8 km/h on all travel lanes, cross-aisles and staging approaches.
3. Across the outdoor yard, limit speed to 15 km/h and adjust further for weather, surface conditions and queuing trailers.
4. Within marked pedestrian zones and crossings, slow to 5 km/h, make eye contact where possible and give way to people on foot.
5. On dock ramps and leveller approaches, travel at no more than 5 km/h with the load uphill on gradients and forks kept low.
6. Through the main transport aisles, which are 4.0 m wide, keep to the right, hold the centre clearance and sound the horn before blind junctions.
7. Inside rack storage aisles, which are 3.0 m wide, proceed at walking pace when turning, stacking or passing open pick faces.
8. Around pedestrians, stop completely if the walkway boundary is unclear, wait for the person to clear and then move off smoothly.
9. Wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving, remain seated under the overhead guard and keep hands, feet and hi-vis clothing inside the profile.
10. Respect rated capacity on every lift: counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t for the high bays.
11. Before lifting, confirm the pallet, including its load, weighs at most 800 kg and check the load chart when attachments or high lift heights reduce capacity.
12. When placing pallets to racking, verify each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg in total and never force a pallet that exceeds beam or height clearance.
13. Maintain fork height 100-150 mm above the floor during travel, tilt the mast slightly back and look in the direction of travel at all times.

Carry only stable and evenly distributed loads. Re-wrap or re-stack a leaning pallet before transport and return damaged pallets for repair rather than lifting them high.

Park only in marked positions with forks lowered, controls in neutral and parking brake applied. Switch off the truck, remove the key and never leave a raised load unattended in an aisle.

title: Aisles and Walkways
text:
1. Maintain segregated traffic routes at all times under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Keep vehicle routes, handling areas and pedestrian routes physically separated. Do not remove, move or obscure floor markings, rails or barriers.

2. Keep main transport aisles clear to their full width. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Do not stage pallets, cages, wrappers or waste in main transport aisles. Stop work and clear the aisle immediately if any object intrudes into the marked lane.

3. Keep rack storage aisles clear to their full width. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Position trucks centrally when entering the aisle. Do not park trucks, leave pallets standing or decant stock inside rack storage aisles except for the active handling task.

4. Use only marked segregated walkways when moving on foot. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Walk inside the marked lines. Do not step into vehicle aisles to overtake, shortcut or inspect stock.

5. Keep all pedestrian walkways free of obstructions along their entire length. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and must remain passable side to side. Remove stretch film, strapping, labels and debris at once. Report damaged flooring, faded lines or missing barrier sections before continuing work.

6. Give way to pedestrians at every marked crossing. Stop the truck before the stop line. Make eye contact with the pedestrian before proceeding. Sound the horn where sight lines are restricted and proceed only when the crossing is fully clear.

7. Wear the required personal protective equipment before entering traffic areas. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Wear the vest fastened and visible at all times. Do not enter aisles, docks or storage areas without it.

8. Wear approved foot protection on the floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Keep footwear laced and in serviceable condition. Replace damaged footwear before starting the shift.

9. Protect walkway edges, rack ends, dock approaches and crossing points. Check that fixed barriers, bollards and handrails are upright and secured. Cordon off any location where protection is damaged and prevent pedestrian access until repair is complete.

10. Stage work so aisles and walkways stay passable. Plan pallet drops, replenishment moves and outbound transfers to avoid blocking main routes. Move one load at a time. Return empty pallets, jacks and packaging materials to their defined positions immediately after use.

11. Inspect routes at the start of work and during the shift. Confirm main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and unobstructed, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide and unobstructed, and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and unobstructed. Clear minor obstructions at once. Escalate blocked fire exits, blocked crossings or structural damage without delay.

12. Enforce PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse consistently. Challenge any person without a high-visibility vest or without Safety footwear class S3. Stop any truck, pallet movement or manual task that forces pedestrians out of the marked walkway. Restore segregation before resuming work.

title: Speed Limits
text:
1. Observe a maximum of 8 km/h for all forklift travel inside the building under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
2. Maintain that indoor limit through every internal area, including receiving, bulk storage, picking, dispatch, cold and value-added zones, without exception for empty travel.
3. Outside the building, drive at no more than 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.
4. Reduce speed progressively when transitioning from the yard through dock openings into internal areas so the 8 km/h indoor limit is already established at the threshold.
5. Slow to 5 km/h in every marked pedestrian zone and at every marked pedestrian crossing under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.
6. Give way to pedestrians at those crossings and proceed only when the route ahead is clear and sightlines are fully confirmed.
7. Apply the same 5 km/h maximum on all dock ramps and leveller approaches, whether travelling laden or unladen.
8. Serving the site are 8 dock doors, with dock doors 1-4 assigned to inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 assigned to outbound dispatch.
9. Approach each of those dock doors at ramp speed, because each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller that creates a gradient, gap and surface change.
10. Inspect the leveller plate position and dock edge before crossing, then cross in a straight line without steering, braking hard or accelerating on the plate itself.
