11. Inside Zone A in front of dock doors 1-4, retain the 8 km/h indoor limit and drop further to 5 km/h wherever pedestrian markings, inspection activity or staged inbound pallets narrow the route.
12. Within Zone D in front of dock doors 5-8, combine the indoor and ramp rules: hold 8 km/h on the staging apron, then 5 km/h on every ramp and leveller approach during loading and outbound movements.
13. Treat any obscured corner, rack end, cold-zone doorway or pedestrian walkway intersection as a pedestrian zone: slow to 5 km/h, sound the horn where fitted, and widen the turn only within the marked traffic lane.
14. Adjust below the posted maxima in wet, cold, congested or low-visibility conditions, and stop completely rather than pass where passage width or stability is in doubt.
15. Report missing, faded or damaged speed and pedestrian-zone markings for replacement, and continue to apply the indoor, yard, pedestrian-zone and ramp limits by location even where markings are temporarily unclear.

title: PPE and Pedestrians
text:
1. Wear a high-visibility vest at all times on the warehouse floor. Check the fastening and condition before entering the operating areas and replace damaged garments immediately through the normal issue route.

2. Wear safety footwear class S3 whenever present on the warehouse floor. Ensure laces are tied, soles are clean, and overshoes or protectors are removed where they would reduce grip.

3. Fasten the seat belt before moving a forklift and keep it fastened whenever the truck is moving. Forklift operators operating forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks shall stop the truck completely before unbuckling for load inspection or dismount.

4. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on every foot movement inside the building and yard. Read the marked floor signs at each crossing and obey the priority rules for trucks and pedestrians without exception.

5. Keep strictly to the segregated pedestrian routes between tasks. Walk inside the marked boundaries, face the direction of truck traffic where the layout allows it, and avoid shortcuts through racking rows or staging areas.

6. Make eye contact with the driver before stepping into any crossing or shared area. Raise a hand to confirm you have been seen, wait for the truck to stop or pass, and cross directly without lingering in the traffic lane.

7. Slow forklifts to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Sound the horn on blind approaches, reduce speed further when visibility is restricted by loads or racking, and yield to pedestrians already on the crossing.

8. Maintain a safe separation from moving trucks while working near traffic. Stand clear of masts, forks and swing areas during lifting, never pass under elevated forks, and remain outside the manoeuvring space until the operator signals completion.

9. Prohibit unauthorised presence in active truck lanes during loading, unloading and replenishment movements. Direct visitors along pedestrian routes only, escort them through shared sections, and stop work if segregation cannot be maintained.

10. Report damaged PPE, missing floor markings, obscured signs and unsafe behaviour immediately. Remain at a safe location while the hazard is assessed and return to the area only after the route or equipment has been released for normal use.

title: Evacuation and Drills
text:
1. Activate PR-14 Emergency evacuation immediately when the fire alarm sounds, when smoke or gas is detected, or when instructed over the PA system.
2. Direct all floor staff to stop work at once and make equipment safe where doing so takes seconds and does not delay escape.
3. Assign wardens to sweep Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E and Zone F, checking toilets, offices and the hazmat cage area for stragglers.
4. Stop all forklift, reach truck and pallet jack movements and lower forks to the floor before abandoning trucks clear of aisles and exits.
5. Leave the building by the nearest marked emergency exit and never use lifts, dock levellers or shortcuts through racking.
6. Walk briskly to the assembly point by the north fence and remain in shift groups for counting.
7. Assemble visitors, drivers and contractors with the shift that received them and report missing persons to the wardens without delay.
8. Conduct roll call at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building.
9. Prohibit re-entry until the shift supervisor confirms the building is safe and releases staff by name or by team.
10. Notify emergency services from the assembly point and meet arriving crews with site plans, access keys and hazmat information.
11. Record names, times, locations and actions taken in the incident report during the standby at the assembly point.
12. Review every incident report following PR-14 Emergency evacuation, since the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
13. File completed reports, roll-call sheets and service attendance notes in the incident file within the same shift.
14. Practise evacuation every quarter through a full drill covering alarm, escape, assembly, roll call and controlled re-entry.
15. Brief all newcomers on escape routes, exits, assembly point location and roll-call discipline before their first task on the floor.
16. Restore normal operations only after headcount reconciliation, area inspection and formal stand-down by the shift supervisor.

title: Incident Response
text:
Respond to every incident on the shift without delay and contain the immediate risk before resuming work.

1. Report any injury, collision, spill, fire alarm, rack damage, dock damage or near miss to the shift supervisor immediately by radio or in person.
2. Secure the affected area with barriers or cones and stop all forklift and pedestrian movement through it until released.
3. Administer first aid within competence and summon emergency services where injury, fire or hazardous release requires external response.
4. Isolate leaking, smoking or unstable loads where safe to do so and ventilate the area without exposing others to harm.
5. Preserve the scene for examination by leaving equipment, pallets and debris in place unless continued danger forces removal.
6. Notify the shift supervisor of names, time, location, equipment involved and witnesses while facts remain fresh.
7. Direct the shift supervisor to take command of floor staff and incident response for the remainder of the shift.
8. Deploy staff to guide arriving responders, maintain segregation of pedestrians and MHE, and protect adjacent stock and aisles.
9. Initiate PR-14 Emergency evacuation where the incident threatens the building, cold-chain integrity or safe egress, and account for all personnel.
10. Complete the incident report on the shift with sequence of events, injuries, damage, immediate actions and photographs where available.
11. Submit every incident report to the shift supervisor for review before end of shift and record any interim controls imposed.
12. Escalate serious injury, major damage, hazmat release or operational shutdown to the warehouse manager on the same shift.

Hold the warehouse manager accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs on incident outcomes. Refer corrective actions, retraining needs, repair requests and procedural changes from the review to that sign-off.

Retain closed reports in the incident file and brief incoming staff on outstanding restrictions during handover. Track repeat events by location, task and equipment type and adjust controls to prevent recurrence.

title: Handover and Shifts
text:
1. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every shift change without exception.

Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Coverage outside those hours requires a specific overtime arrangement.

2. Place responsibility for the handover with the outgoing supervisor.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Outgoing and incoming shift supervisors must meet on the floor for the handover. Never conduct the handover by phone, note, or message alone.

3. Confirm staffing and equipment status face to face.

During PR-15 End-of-shift handover, state the number of staff present, absent, and reassigned. Report trucks held for maintenance, docks blocked, and scanners missing from the charging rack. Incoming supervisors must acknowledge each point before accepting the floor.

4. Review work-in-progress across all zones.

Describe inbound trailers waiting, pallets held for booking, replenishment tasks still open, picking tasks incomplete, packed pallets staged, and loads awaiting collection. Identify quarantine holdings requiring review. Highlight cold-chain and hazmat issues separately so nothing carries over unseen.

5. Manually verify cold-zone temperature as part of every handover.

Cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift. Record the reading, the time, and the initials of the person taking it. Where the reading lies outside the required band, escalate immediately under the cold-chain procedure and note the escalation in the handover record. Outgoing supervisors remain responsible until the incoming supervisor signs acceptance of the temperature record.

6. Control overtime strictly through senior approval.

Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Shift supervisors must not promise, authorise, or work additional hours without that approval. Submit each request with reason, hours, headcount, and cost centre before the overtime starts. Attach the approval to the handover record when overtime extends either Shift 1 running 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 running 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

7. Close the handover with a signed record.

Both shift supervisors must sign and date the PR-15 End-of-shift handover log. File open actions with named owners and deadlines. Brief floor staff on priorities for the next shift within the first minutes after takeover. Retain the completed log for audit and make it available to the warehouse manager on request.

title: Forklift Operating Rules
text:
1. Operate handling equipment only under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and only within your authorisation. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.

2. Do not drive any powered truck without written authorisation. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

3. Understand the accountability behind this rule. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

4. Know the fleet before you book a truck. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts.

5. Respect rated capacities on every lift. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t.

6. Use the correct truck in the high bays. The fleet has 4 reach trucks for the high bays.

7. Never exceed the rated capacity of the assigned truck. Reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t.

8. Select the right pallet jack for the task and floor. The fleet has 8 electric pallet jacks.

9. Report defects on hand equipment immediately. The site has 12 hand pallet jacks.

10. Complete the documented pre-use check every day. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.

11. Observe the correct order for the daily check. The daily forklift check happens BEFORE first use each day.

12. Do not start the shift on an unchecked truck. Confirm the daily record is signed before switching on.

13. Wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.

14. Limit speed inside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

15. Control speed in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

16. Slow to walking pace where pedestrians have priority. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings.

17. Approach level edges at low speed. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

18. Adjust speed further for load, visibility and floor condition. Stop and sound the horn where sight lines are restricted.

19. Park only in designated positions with forks lowered, brake applied and power isolated. Hand over keys only to authorised operators.

title: Pedestrian Walkways and Crossings
text:
1. Walk only inside the segregated pedestrian walkways when moving through the warehouse. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are marked for foot traffic only.

2. Wear a high-visibility vest at all times on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, including visitors and office staff crossing to the zones.

3. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor and applies on walkways, in aisles and at crossings.

4. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse to every movement on foot between Zone A, Zone B, Zone C and Zone D. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

5. Keep to the walkway side when passing Zone B. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Do not step into rack storage aisles unless your task requires access, and check both directions before entering.

6. Cross main transport aisles only at marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Stop at the marking, establish eye contact with the driver, and wait until the truck has stopped.

7. Expect forklifts to slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Do not cross behind a reversing truck. Continue to watch for a second truck in the adjacent lane.

8. Observe the indoor limit during all crossings. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. Never assume a driver has seen you, even where the 8 km/h limit applies.

9. Stay clear of dock ramps and leveller approaches unless authorised to work there. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Use only the marked pedestrian route to reach the dock areas.

10. Plan picking movements in Zone C to minimise crossing. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Push pallet jacks within the pick aisle and park them clear of the walkway edge.

11. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation at every interface with pedestrians. Give way to loaded trucks at crossings. Keep hands clear of racking and keep walkways free of pallets, film and strapping.

12. Report blocked walkways, faded markings, damaged barriers or lighting faults to the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Do not move barrier tape or enter a closed walkway until it is released.

title: Yard and Dock Safety
text:
1. Limit forklift speed to 15 km/h in the outdoor yard at all times.
2. Reduce speed to 8 km/h immediately on entering the building enclosure.
3. Slow to 5 km/h through every marked pedestrian zone and crossing on yard routes and dock approaches.
4. Approach all dock ramps and leveller approaches at no more than 5 km/h with the load low and forward visibility maintained.
5. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all yard driving, reversing, parking and coupling manoeuvres without exception.
6. Observe PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse where yard footways meet dock stairs, offices and crossing points.
7. Recognise the building has 8 dock doors, each fitted with its own dock leveller.
8. Direct inbound vehicles only to dock doors 1-4 for receiving.
9. Unload inbound trailers in Zone A, the receiving zone for unloading and goods inspection in front of docks 1-4.
10. Stage outbound trailers only at dock doors 5-8 for dispatch.
11. Hold outbound pallets and staged loads in Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
12. Obtain dispatcher assignment before moving any vehicle to a door.
13. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads.
14. Wait for the dispatcher to assign dock doors and time slots to carriers before admitting vehicles to the gate or apron.
15. Prohibit reversing toward an open dock edge unless guides, mirrors and audible warning devices are in use.
16. Inspect the leveller, dock seal, wheel chocks and trailer bed before placing the first pallet.
17. Confirm the trailer is braked, chocked and supported before driving a forklift onto the bed.
18. Keep forklift forks clear of leveller lips, dock edges and door tracks during alignment.
19. Yield to banksmen and pedestrians at all dock corners, roller doors and yard junctions.
20. Sound the horn before exiting the building into the yard and before entering the building from the yard.
21. Park MHE clear of dock approaches, levellers and emergency routes when not loading.
22. Report faulty levellers, damaged doors, uneven yard surfaces or defective lighting for immediate repair.

title: Mandatory PPE
text:
1. Wear a high-visibility vest at all times on the warehouse floor.
2. Keep the vest fastened and visible over outer clothing during every task.
3. Put on safety footwear class S3 before entering the floor area.
4. Ensure footwear remains laced, intact and suitable for truck and pedestrian areas.
5. Fasten the seat belt whenever the forklift truck is moving.
6. Confirm belt adjustment and locking before starting travel under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
7. Observe pedestrian separation and visibility rules under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.
8. Report missing, damaged or non-compliant protective equipment without delay.
9. Replace any soiled vest that no longer provides clear visibility.
10. Exchange any footwear showing split seams, exposed toecaps or failed soles.
11. Stop truck operation immediately if the seat belt is defective and hand over the truck for repair.
12. Refuse access to the floor to any person without correct vest and footwear.

The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Enforcement of vest, footwear and seat-belt compliance forms part of that accountability, including provision of compliant stocks and authorisation of replacements. Visitors, contractors and drivers under escort remain subject to the same vest and footwear obligation while on the floor, without exception for short visits.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Supervisors check compliance at shift start, during patrols and after any incident or near miss. Correct any breach on the spot by stopping the task, directing the person to obtain compliant equipment and recording the intervention where required for follow-up.

Within PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, seat-belt use is inseparable from authorised truck operation. Never override, disconnect or pad the belt switch. Keep the belt clean and retractable, and test retraction during the daily check sequence. Supervisors exclude from driving duties any operator who repeatedly fails to wear the belt.

Within PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, high-visibility vests and safety footwear class S3 provide the baseline protection that makes segregation and crossing controls effective. Pedestrians enhance their own conspicuity by keeping vests closed, avoiding covering them with bags or radios, and by maintaining footwear in serviceable condition for grip and impact protection.

Treat repeated non-compliance as a safety breach for incident reporting and retraining. Supervisors escalate persistent violations through the site safety chain for formal action. Managers review compliance trends and ensure that supply, sizing and replacement arrangements keep every shift fully equipped.

title: Racking and Stacking Limits
text:
1. Store all bulk reserve pallets only in Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking.
2. Plan all put-away against the available capacity of the high-bay racking, which provides 2,400 pallet positions, and never create overflow stacks in aisles or at rack ends.
3. Weigh every assignment before placement. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg.
4. Load each rack bay to at most 2,700 kg in total. Calculate the bay total as the sum of all pallet levels in that bay, not per level alone.
5. Distribute weight evenly across beams and uprights. Place heavier pallets at lower levels and never concentrate full-weight pallets on a single side of a bay.
6. Use equipment within its rating when loading racks. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks for the high bays are rated at 1.6 t.
7. Set down pallets squarely on both support beams. Stop placement immediately if a pallet overhangs, rocks, or rests on damaged timber, and re-palletise before re-attempting.
8. Keep free block-stacked pallets outside racking to a maximum of 3 pallets high.
9. Keep free block-stacked pallets to a maximum of 4.0 m in height. Apply both limits together; stop at whichever limit is reached first.
10. Build block stacks only on level, sound flooring, in straight vertical columns. Leave no leaning stacks, no mixed footprints, and no damaged pallets at the base.
11. Remove from service any rack showing bent uprights, cracked welds, missing safety pins, or beam deflection. Barrier the bay off and report it for repair without delay.
12. Support the monthly racking programme. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.
13. Allow the maintenance technician full access for that inspection. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.
14. Record every inspection finding, repair, and release back to use in the racking log. Do not reload a repaired bay until the documented release is signed.
15. Treat any fallen goods, crushed cartons, or impact damage as a load-safety event. Isolate the stock and apply PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
16. Escalate any collapse risk, overload doubt, or repeated rack impact to senior control. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

title: Daily Checks and Maintenance
text:
1. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation to every truck, leveller and jack on site without exception.

Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks, and no other person may take those trucks into operation. The fleet under this instruction comprises 6 electric counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks for the high bays, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.

2. Complete the documented pre-use check on each forklift before first use each day.

Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day, even if it was checked on the previous shift and shows no visible defect. Do not start the engine, raise the forks or accept a transport task until the daily check sheet is signed and filed for that truck.

3. Examine brakes, steering, horn, lights, tyres, forks, chains, hydraulics and battery charge during the daily check.

Record any warning lamp, fluid leak, unusual noise or structural damage immediately on the check sheet. Remove a defective truck from service at once and prevent further use until release is documented.

4. Check reach trucks for high-bay functions in addition to the standard truck examination.

Test side-shift, tilt, reach extension and height limitation before entering the racking aisles. Report any drift, judder or loss of lifting accuracy before lifting above ground level.

5. Inspect electric and hand pallet jacks before the shift starts.

Verify emergency stop, tiller operation, lifting and lowering, wheels and forks on the 8 electric pallet jacks. Verify handle, pump action, release valve and load wheels on the 12 hand pallet jacks, and withdraw damaged units from the floor.

6. Obtain warehouse-manager authorisation before operating any forklift or reach truck.

Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators, and authorisation must be in place before keys are issued. Do not permit unsupervised operation, loan of keys or use of trucks outside the authorised category.

7. Maintain all MHE, racking and dock equipment through the maintenance function and log every repair.

The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs with date, equipment identity, fault found and action taken. Keep the log available for inspection and close no job without a recorded outcome.

8. Inspect each of the 8 dock doors and its dock leveller on a planned basis.

Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller, and both elements must be kept free, level and fully operational. Prohibit loading or unloading at any door where the leveller, seal, lights or restraint show a fault, and notify maintenance without delay.

9. Submit racking to a documented safety inspection every month.

Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month covering uprights, beams, bracing, fixings, load notices and clearance. Isolate any damaged bay immediately, unload if so instructed, and prevent re-use until repair and sign-off are recorded.

10. Keep daily check sheets and monthly racking reports in the designated file for audit.

File the pre-use checks by truck and date, and file the racking inspections by zone and month. Present missing or incomplete records as a non-conformance at handover.

title: Working in the Cold Zone
text:
1. Follow PR-12 Cold-chain handling for every entry, work task and exit involving chilled stock.
2. Understand Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
3. Keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times during storage, handling and door movements.
4. Sustain the cold zone at or below +8 °C without exception during storage, handling and door movements.
5. Check the cold-zone temperature manually each shift with the designated calibrated instrument.
6. Record each manual verification immediately in the temperature log with time, reading and initials.
7. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and completes its own manual verification before handover.
8. Subsequently Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, and completes its own separate manual verification.
9. Alert the shift supervisor immediately about any reading outside +2 to +8 °C, failed verification or suspect stock.
10. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
11. Wear high-visibility vests mandatorily for everyone on the warehouse floor, including all work inside Zone E.
12. Use safety footwear class S3 mandatorily on the warehouse floor, including all work inside Zone E.
13. Minimise cold exposure by planning picks, put-away and checks before entering Zone E.
14. Rotate personnel sensibly between chilled and ambient tasks to reduce prolonged cold exposure.
15. Consume warm fluids and use designated warming areas outside Zone E during natural pauses in chilled work.
16. Dry any condensation on floors, packaging and handling equipment promptly to prevent slips and label damage.
17. Close cold-zone doors and curtains immediately after each pass to protect temperature stability and product safety.
18. Prohibit propping cold-zone doors open for convenience or for staging pallets in the doorway.
19. Inspect chilled pallets for frost damage, wet cartons and unreadable labels before moving them onward.
20. Isolate questionable chilled stock in its location and escalate it through PR-12 Cold-chain handling rather than dispatching it.
21. Coordinate door traffic courteously to avoid queues with open doors and idling handling equipment inside Zone E.

title: Hazmat Storage Limits
text:
1. Store all hazardous materials only inside the hazmat cage. Do not place hazmat in bulk storage, in picking faces, on dock staging areas, or in general floor locations.

2. Locate the cage in Zone F. Zone F holds the value-added services area, and the hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2. Keep its boundaries, gates and ventilation clear at all times.

3. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to every receipt, put-away, issue, relocation and inspection involving the cage. Do not use any alternative method.

4. Never exceed 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Treat 4,000 kg as a hard ceiling for the combined weight of all packages, pallets, drums and containers present.

5. Control intake against the ceiling before accepting any delivery. Check the recorded cage balance, add the inbound weight, and refuse or reschedule the put-away if the total would pass 4,000 kg.

6. Limit pallet weight inside the cage. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg. Reject overweight pallets for repacking or splitting outside the cage.

7. Plan cage capacity on full-weight pallets. The hazmat cage holds at most 5 full-weight pallets. Do not attempt to fit a sixth 800 kg pallet by rearranging, double-stacking or using the margins of the 60 m2 area.

8. Keep mixed lighter pallets within the same kilogram limit. Count the actual kilograms on the system record, not the number of pallets alone, and stop loading when the sum reaches 4,000 kg.

9. Segregate incompatible classes inside the cage according to PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Maintain separation distances, use bunded positions where specified, and keep labels facing the access aisle.

10. Inspect every package before placement. Reject leaking, swollen, corroded, torn or unlabelled units, and remove suspect stock from Zone F through the defined spill and quarantine route.

11. Record every hazmat receipt, issue and relocation on the same shift. Keep the running balance visible so the next put-away can be checked against the 4,000 kg limit without delay.

12. Verify the cage total daily. Reconcile any difference before further put-away, and hold further inbound hazmat outside Zone F until the balance is confirmed.

13. Report overstock, damage, leakage or ventilation failure immediately. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Escalate cage exceedances and unsafe conditions to the warehouse manager without waiting for the next shift.

14. Prohibit smoking, hot work, charging of trucks and storage of non-hazmat goods inside the 60 m2 cage. Keep fire access, spill kits and safety notices unobstructed and legible.

title: Spills and Damaged Goods
text:
1. Stop work around any spill or fallen load and secure the immediate area against forklift and pedestrian movement.
2. Put on high-visibility vests before entering the affected area, as high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
3. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor during the entire spill response and damaged-goods handling operation.
4. Execute PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for every chemical, oil, chilled-liquid or unknown-substance spill without deviation.
5. Contain liquids with the nearest spill kit, prevent entry into drains and aisles, and ventilate the area where the procedure requires it.
6. Never touch, repack or move leaking hazmat containers with bare hands and never place suspect containers into normal storage.
7. Alert the shift supervisor immediately after containment, since the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
8. Execute PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for crushed cartons, broken pallets, torn wrapping, wet stock and any goods contaminated by a spill.
9. Photograph the damage, record product, quantity, location, time and suspected cause, and keep the pallet intact for inspection.
10. Transfer all goods awaiting a damaged-goods decision to the quarantine area in Zone F and do not restock, rework or scrap them there.
11. Mark the quarantined pallet clearly with damage details and prevent any further movement until a written decision exists.
12. Obtain approval for the write-off before posting it in the system, in line with PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
13. Submit write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor, who approves damaged-goods write-offs up to that value.
14. Escalate write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager, since damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.
15. Understand that the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR and no other role may substitute that sign-off.
16. Hand over open spill clean-ups and quarantined pallets at shift change with quantities, locations and actions taken fully documented.
17. Reinspect the cleaned floor, racking and adjacent stock for hidden damage before releasing the area back to normal operation.
18. Replace used spill materials, report depleted kits for replenishment, and confirm that quarantined stock remains segregated in Zone F.

title: Incident Reporting
text:
1. Report every injury, collision, rack damage, dock damage, fire alarm activation and near miss at once to the supervisor on duty. Do not wait until the end of the task and do not leave the scene unsafe.

2. Notify the shift supervisor directly by radio or in person. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Follow the instructions given and preserve the area for inspection where safe to do so.

3. Record the incident in the incident report before leaving the floor. State time, place, persons involved, equipment involved, witnesses and a factual description of what happened. Attach photographs where the reporting form provides for them.

4. Submit every incident report for review without delay. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Correct incomplete reports immediately when they are returned and resubmit them within the same duty period.

5. Escalate serious injury, major damage, operational shutdown and any release covered by PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to the warehouse manager through the shift supervisor. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

6. Treat damaged stock only under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Segregate affected pallets and cartons, label them clearly and prevent further movement until a disposition decision is recorded.

7. Obtain write-off approval before posting any damaged-goods write-off. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. Send larger cases to the warehouse manager with the inspection record and photographs attached.

8. Observe the 500 EUR threshold strictly. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR. Do not split one damage event into smaller amounts to avoid the higher approval.

9. Include open incidents, damaged-goods cases and spill follow-up actions in PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Brief the incoming shift supervisor face to face on injuries, blocked locations, quarantined stock and equipment taken out of service.

10. Check that the handover log records report numbers, approver names and pending actions. Carry forward any incident without supervisor review or without required write-off approval as an outstanding item for the next shift.

11. Cooperate fully with investigation and remedial actions. Provide statements on request, attend re-briefing when ordered and apply revised controls from the first task after they are issued.

title: Evacuation and Re-entry
text:
1. Apply PR-14 Emergency evacuation on every alarm, confirmed fire, gas release, structural failure or instruction from the shift supervisor to leave the building.
2. Stop all work immediately when the alarm sounds. Shut down equipment only where it can be done without delay and never return for personal belongings, scanners or paperwork.
3. Leave by the nearest safe escape route. Keep to the marked pedestrian routes, assist visitors and contractors in your area, and close doors behind you without locking them.
4. Proceed directly to the designated assembly point and remain there. Do not wait near dock doors, gather in the yard traffic lanes or re-enter to search for colleagues.
5. Report to the shift supervisor for roll call on arrival at the assembly point. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and directs headcount reconciliation for everyone present during Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
6. Give your name, work area and any information about persons still inside, last known location and nature of the emergency. Notify any injury, missing person or hazard observed during escape without leaving the assembly area.
7. Wait for further instruction after reporting. Keep the assembly area clear for emergency services, maintain silence during roll call, and follow only directions issued through the shift supervisor chain.
8. Understand that roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building (PR-14). No individual, group or vehicle may enter until the roll call is complete and the building is formally released.
9. Re-enter only when explicitly cleared. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and release for normal work follows confirmation that conditions are safe.
10. Attend the quarterly evacuation drill as scheduled. An evacuation drill runs every quarter to test alarms, routes, assembly discipline and roll-call accuracy across both shifts.
11. Treat each drill as a real evacuation under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Evacuate fully, assemble promptly, participate in roll call and remain until stood down.
12. Report defects found during evacuation or drill, including blocked exits, failed alarms, unclear markings, lighting faults and congestion points. Remain available for debriefing and repeat any task as directed to close the exercise.

title: Safety Roles and Handover
text:
1. Recognise the warehouse manager as accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Escalate any matter beyond shift authority to that level without delay.

2. On every shift, follow the shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Direct all immediate safety decisions, task priorities and emergency actions through the supervisor on duty.

3. Understand the daily operating rhythm. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Plan handovers, inspections and incident follow-up around that window.

4. Continue the same discipline into the afternoon. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Ensure continuity of supervision, open tasks and safety controls across the changeover.

5. Submit every incident report to the shift supervisor for review. Include injuries, collisions, spills, alarms, rack or dock damage and near misses with times, locations and witnesses.

6. Never operate a forklift without proper authority. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. Present licences, training records and written authorisation before issuing keys or tasks.

7. Coordinate all vehicle movements through the assigned owner. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Obtain the door allocation before staging, loading or unloading.

8. Keep returns decisions within the defined authority. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Do not restock, rework or scrap goods awaiting decision until that approval is recorded.

9. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every change between Shift 1 and Shift 2. Meet face to face on the floor and walk through staffing, equipment status, cold-zone readings, quarantine holds, dock activity and open incidents.

10. Document the handover fully before leaving the floor. Record outstanding risks, faulty equipment positions, incomplete counts and pending approvals. Confirm both outgoing and incoming supervisors understand who owns each action until the next handover.

11. Carry unresolved safety matters forward explicitly. Where an incident review, returns disposition or dock rescheduling remains open, name the owner, the next step and the deadline. Leave no shift to assume another team has closed the risk.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
1. Remain accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs across the warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 with 8 dock doors.
2. Direct all inbound flow through Zone A as the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, where Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving.
3. Control bulk inventory in Zone B as the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, together with Zone C as the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
4. Supervise Zone D as the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, where Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.
5. Govern Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, ensuring the cold zone stays at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C with manual verification each shift.
6. Own Zone F as the value-added services area, containing the hazmat cage inside Zone F covering 60 m2, the quarantine area in Zone F, and returns inspection in Zone F.
7. Enforce the hazmat ceiling of no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat stored in the hazmat cage at one time, equivalent to at most 5 full-weight pallets where a pallet including its load may weigh at most 800 kg.
8. Authorise inventory integrity through PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts: sign off stocktake results exclusively, with cycle counts running every working day on a rotating zone schedule and a full wall-to-wall stocktake once a year.
9. Decide damaged-goods expenditure under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling: approve write-offs above 500 EUR, while the shift supervisor approves write-offs up to 500 EUR and runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
10. Release resourcing and competence: approve overtime solely, and authorise new forklift operators solely before any operation under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.
11. Delegate defined authorities and retain oversight: the shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling and reviews every incident report, while the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.
12. Maintain prescribed site routines across Shift 1 running 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday and Shift 2 running 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, requiring high-visibility vests for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor.
13. Answer for end-to-end compliance across PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, PR-04 Order picking, PR-05 Packing and labelling, PR-06 Outbound dispatch, PR-07 Returns handling, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, PR-12 Cold-chain handling, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, PR-14 Emergency evacuation and PR-15 End-of-shift handover.

Across all zones the manager sets standards, confirms resources and closes escalations from shift leadership. No other role assumes the reserved sign-offs for stocktake results, write-offs above threshold, overtime or forklift authorisation.

title: Shift Supervisors
text:
1. Run one shift: floor staff and incident response across all zones during the assigned hours. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

2. Report to the warehouse manager, who remains accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Escalate beyond delegated authority without delay.

3. Direct work in Zone A, the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection; Zone B, the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking; Zone C, the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks; Zone D, the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8; Zone E, the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C; and Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.

4. Coordinate with the dispatcher on door use. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers; do not reassign confirmed inbound or outbound doors without dispatcher agreement.

5. Enforce floor discipline to PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Require high-visibility vests for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor, and stop unsafe pedestrian or equipment interaction immediately.

6. Own cold-chain supervision for the shift under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Ensure cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift. Keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C, and act on any deviation per procedure.

7. Supervise hazmat activity under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. Ensure no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat is stored in the hazmat cage at one time, and halt further put-away if the limit would be exceeded.

8. Approve delegated decisions promptly. Under PR-07 Returns handling, approve the final disposition of inspected returns. Under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR; damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval and must be forwarded with evidence.

9. Support inventory accuracy without exceeding authority. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. A full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results; the supervisor ensures counters are assigned, areas are accessible, and recounts are completed.

10. Lead immediate response under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Account for shift staff at the assembly point, where roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building. Support the evacuation drill, which runs every quarter, and ensure newcomers know routes and muster arrangements.

11. Review every incident report for the shift. Investigate causes, arrange containment and corrective action, and forward overtime needs upward, since only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.

12. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover to the next supervisor. Hand over staffing, door status, cold-chain status, hazmat balance, quarantine holds, open incidents, and pending approvals, leaving the floor in a safe and controlled state for the incoming shift.

title: Dispatchers
text:
1. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads across both daily shifts.
2. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday; dispatch cover continues through handover without gaps.
3. The building has 8 dock doors, each fitted with a dock leveller.
4. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving in Zone A, the receiving zone for unloading and goods inspection.
5. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch from Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
6. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for loading.
7. Allocation of all dock doors and carrier time slots rests with the dispatcher, who balances inbound arrivals under PR-01 Inbound receiving against outbound departures under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
8. At receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading; dispatchers enforce that sequence in the booking and arrival instructions.
9. Packing output from PR-05 Packing and labelling is accepted only as staged, wrapped pallets for Zone D.
10. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers; no unwrapped pallet is released for loading.
11. Every pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg; dispatch plans all loads against that ceiling.
12. Contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 22000 kg with 33 floor pallet positions.
13. A trailer therefore takes at most 27 full-weight pallets, limited by payload before floor positions are reached.
14. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg with 6 pallet positions.
15. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
16. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
17. Outbound capacity is at most 324 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated from doors, loads per shift and pallets per trailer.
18. Release decisions verify wrapping, count, door, vehicle and documentation before the trailer or van is authorised to depart.
19. Coordination with the shift supervisor, who runs one shift including floor staff and incident response, keeps loading labour, MHE and staging aligned to the door plan.
20. Escalation for operations, safety and final sign-offs goes to the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. Unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A under PR-01 Inbound receiving.
2. Staff Zone A, the receiving zone for inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Accept vehicles only at dock doors 1-4, which serve inbound receiving.
3. Cover Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, as rostered by the shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
4. Wear high-visibility vests at all times on the warehouse floor. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor without exception.
5. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on all movements between dock, inspection lane and staging.
6. Execute the document check BEFORE unloading at receiving. Compare delivery notes, purchase orders and vehicle identity against the booking, then authorise dock unloading.
7. Unload pallets with the 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks provided. Reject any pallet, including its load, weighing more than 800 kg and report the overweight to the shift supervisor.
8. Inspect inbound goods BEFORE they are booked into the system. Record counts, batch data, expiry dates, damage and label condition using the shared pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners.
9. Book inspected goods into the system strictly BEFORE put-away to storage. Hand released ambient pallets to PR-02 Put-away to storage for transfer to Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking.
10. Handle chilled products under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Direct controlled goods to Zone E, the cold zone for chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Respect that the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C.
11. Route cartons needing additional handling to Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, after system booking.
12. Escalate shortages, overages, damage and temperature deviations to the shift supervisor on the same shift. Observe that the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

title: Pickers
text:
1. Pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks and complete only the lines directed by the system.
2. Work in Zone C, the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks, and draw no reserve stock directly from Zone B, the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
3. Start picking only after pick faces have been replenished under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces; pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts.
4. Operate on Shift 1 running 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or on Shift 2 running 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, reporting to the shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
5. Recognise that the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and escalate stoppages and systemic shortages beyond shift authority.
6. Collect one of the 20 handheld WMS scanners shared by pickers and inbound staff at shift start, log on with personal ID, and operate equipment only within training and authorisation.
7. Follow PR-04 Order picking for every task: confirm location, quantity and batch on the scanner, pick in the prescribed sequence, and maintain location accuracy and stock rotation as directed.
8. Scan-verify every picked item BEFORE packing, in line with PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling; picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing.
9. Pack, label and hand over completed picks for transfer to Zone D, the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, and never stage packed work in picking aisles.
10. Use the 12 hand pallet jacks only for their intended cage and tote movements in Zone C, park them clear of aisles and walkways, and report faults rather than continuing with defective equipment.
11. Wear high-visibility vests, mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, and safety footwear class S3, mandatory on the warehouse floor, at all times in Zones B, C and D.
12. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at pick faces, crossings and shared aisles: keep to segregated routes, make eye contact with truck operators, and never enter a racking aisle under active replenishment.
13. Coordinate with put-away and replenishment flows under PR-02 Put-away to storage and PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces; do not pick from a face flagged empty, damaged or under replenishment until the system releases it.
14. Report short pick faces, damaged stock, label defects and scanner discrepancies immediately through the prescribed exception process and await instruction before substituting or short-closing a line.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
1. Operate counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks for put-away, replenishment, loading and yard movements as directed by the shift supervisor. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Work Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

2. Obtain written authorisation before operating any powered truck. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

3. Complete the documented pre-use check every day before first use of the assigned truck. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. Report defects immediately and do not use faulty equipment.

4. Drive the fleet within rated capacities and designated areas. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.

5. Observe posted speed limits at all times. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

6. Wear required personal protection on the warehouse floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.

7. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse when travelling on main transport aisles, in racking and near walkways. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Give way to pedestrians at crossings and maintain clear sightlines.

8. Serve all functional zones according to tasking. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.

9. Stage and collect outbound loads only as instructed. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Handle chilled pallets for Zone E under instruction.

10. Respect stacking and racking limits on every lift. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg, and a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg.

11. Follow PR-12 Cold-chain handling for movements in and out of the cold zone. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C, with cold-zone temperature manually verified each shift.

12. Follow PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any cage movement. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, which holds at most 5 full-weight pallets, and never exceed the authorised balance.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. Work permanently in Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, covering returns inspection, packing, labelling, rework and quarantine control.
2. Attend either Shift 1, which runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2, which runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, under the direction of the shift supervisor.
3. Recognise that the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, while the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
4. Wear high-visibility vests at all times on the warehouse floor, together with safety footwear class S3 as mandatory floor personal protective equipment.
5. Execute PR-07 Returns handling for every return delivered for inspection in Zone F.
6. Verify elapsed time against the returns acceptance rule before opening, sorting or assessing any goods, since returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery.
7. Inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap for each line, recording condition, quantity, batch and reason with photographs where required.
8. Apply the fixed sequence of PR-07 without exception: returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision.
9. Retain goods awaiting decision in the quarantine area in Zone F, keep the area segregated and labelled, and submit every proposal for final disposition to the shift supervisor.
10. Accept that the shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns, and transfer approved goods only after that approval is recorded in the system.
11. Carry out PR-05 Packing and labelling to customer and transport requirements, including scan verification, carton building, void fill, sealing, labelling and wrapping without omission.
12. Operate dispatch packing equipment safely and economically, using the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers for all outbound pallets and feeding clean waste card to the site cardboard baler.
13. Confirm that a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg before wrapping, staging or releasing any packed pallet.
14. Segregate shortages, damages and unreadable barcodes found during packing at the pack bench, and route damaged goods through PR-09 Damaged-goods handling into the quarantine area in Zone F.
15. Support PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response only as instructed and trained, respecting that the hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2.
16. Monitor cage discipline during Zone F work and alert the shift supervisor immediately if stock approaches the limit, since no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
17. Maintain housekeeping, segregation and traceability across all Zone F benches, wrappers, baler surroundings and quarantine locations, and hand over open returns and packing tasks fully at each shift change.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. Own inventory accuracy across all storage locations, including cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Coordinate daily counting activity so book stock matches physical stock without interrupting operations.
2. Execute PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts on every working day on a rotating zone schedule. Plan the rotating sequence to cover Zone B, Zone E, the hazmat cage and all other holdings in turn.
3. Prepare the annual full wall-to-wall stocktake. Freeze movements as instructed, brief counters, issue count sheets and scanner tasks, and consolidate results for final review.
4. Enforce the recount rule without exception. Ensure a second count happens before any stock adjustment is posted, and submit verified adjustments through the defined approval route.
5. Accept that only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and no stocktake closes without that sign-off.
6. Work the site shift pattern as rostered. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. Liaise with the shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
7. Control Zone B bulk storage discipline. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, with 2,400 pallet positions in the high-bay racking. Verify locations, labels and quantities during each count.
8. Check bay loading compliance during counts. Record any bay exceeding its limit and escalate for immediate correction. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg.
9. Verify cold-chain holdings under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Confirm the cold zone stays at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C, and manually verify cold-zone temperature each shift.
10. Verify hazmat holdings under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. Confirm no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat is stored in the hazmat cage at one time, equivalent to at most 5 full-weight pallets, and escalate any exceedance.
11. Support PR-09 Damaged-goods handling from the inventory side. Identify damaged stock during counts, secure correct system status, and route write-off proposals to the correct approver. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, given by the warehouse manager.
12. Use the shared pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners for all count, recount and adjustment transactions. Return devices to charge after use and report faults promptly.
13. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor at all times. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. Maintain all materials handling, storage and dock equipment across Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

2. Own the fleet defined for this site: 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks, 12 hand pallet jacks, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers used by dispatch, 1 cardboard baler, 8 dock doors each fitted with a dock leveller, and 20 handheld WMS scanners shared by pickers and inbound staff. Keep every unit available, charged, clean and safe for use.

3. Support PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Verify that every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. Enforce the rule that the daily forklift check happens before first use each day. Remove from service any truck with an unresolved fault until repair and release are recorded.

4. Maintain Zone B as the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking. Service the high-bay racking that provides 2,400 pallet positions. Ensure each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg and load notices remain legible at every bay.

5. Complete the documented racking safety inspection every month. Examine uprights, beams, bracing, fixings and clearances, confirm repairs, and record the inspection result in the repair log. Isolate damaged bays until signed off.

6. Support PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Maintain refrigeration plant, doors, seals and alarms serving the cold zone. Preserve conditions that keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C. Attend failed verifications when cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.

7. Maintain the hazmat cage inside Zone F. The cage covers 60 m2 and holds no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat at one time. Keep ventilation, bunding, racking, signage, lighting and fire equipment serviceable. Report overstock, damage, leakage or ventilation failure without delay.

8. Log all repairs with date, equipment identity, fault found, parts used, action taken and release status. Keep logs complete and retrievable for audit. Escalate faults affecting safety, cold-chain integrity or dock availability to the shift supervisor who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.

9. Refer final sign-offs for major damage, operational shutdowns and authorisations beyond delegated limits to the warehouse manager who is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

10. Wear high-visibility vests as mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Wear safety footwear class S3 as mandatory on the warehouse floor. Apply lock-off and isolation before working on electrical, hydraulic or elevated equipment.

title: Common Standards for All Roles
text:
1. Report on every shift to the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2. Recognise the warehouse manager as accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
3. Work the rostered pattern of Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
4. Obtain overtime only with prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
5. Wear mandatory personal protective equipment on the warehouse floor at all times.
6. Wear high-visibility vests, mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, kept fastened and clean.
7. Wear safety footwear class S3, mandatory on the warehouse floor, with no exemptions for office visitors.
8. Know the site layout and keep to authorised areas for your task and training.
9. Observe that Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.
10. Observe that Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
11. Observe that Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
12. Observe that Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
13. Observe that Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
14. Observe that Zone F holds the value-added services area, including returns inspection, quarantine and hazmat storage.
15. Use the building with 8 dock doors only as directed: dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch.
16. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on all movements between zones, docks and welfare facilities.
17. Respect materials handling equipment at all times and never assume priority as a pedestrian.
18. Remember forklift limits: forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.
19. Remember forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.
20. Give way where forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings.
21. Keep clear where forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
22. Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation whether you operate equipment or work alongside it.
23. Accept that only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.
24. Support the rule that every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day, since the daily forklift check happens before first use each day.
25. Wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, if authorised as a forklift operator.
26. Report rack damage, dock damage or unsafe storage immediately and respect barriers; racking gets a documented safety inspection every month.
27. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling when entering, working in or receiving from Zone E.
28. Protect product by keeping the cold zone at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C.
29. Record the cold-zone temperature as rostered, since cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
30. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response whenever hazmat is present, spilled or suspected.
31. Know the hazmat cage is inside Zone F, covers 60 m2, and holds no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat at one time.
32. Never enter the cage, move hazmat or start clean-up without authorisation and appropriate instruction.
33. Handle returns within policy: returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery and returns are inspected in Zone F.
34. Respect segregation: the quarantine area is in Zone F for goods awaiting decision.
35. Take part in PR-14 Emergency evacuation training, alarms and headcounts on every shift.
36. Attend the evacuation drill, which runs every quarter, and follow wardens without delay.
37. Assemble as directed, since roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
38. Attend PR-15 End-of-shift handover as required and pass complete, accurate information to the next holder of your task.

title: Receiving Hours, Doors and Intake
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. accepts inbound deliveries in Zone A, the receiving zone covering inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, under PR-01 Inbound receiving.
2. The building provides 8 dock doors in total, with dock doors 1-4 dedicated to inbound receiving and unavailable for outbound loading during receiving hours.
3. Receiving operates across Shift 1 from 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 from 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, ensuring daytime and evening intake cover.
4. Outside those windows no routine unloading is committed, and late or early arrivals will be rescheduled to the next available receiving slot.
5. All carrier arrivals require a pre-booked slot, since the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.
6. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, and for inbound this commitment means controlled door allocation rather than first-come service.
7. Upon arrival at Zone A the driver reports to receiving with delivery documents and vehicle details for verification.
8. In accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading, and no vehicle seal is broken or pallet moved until paperwork matches the booking.
9. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A once documents are cleared for unloading.
10. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, and receiving commits sufficient scanner availability in Zone A to avoid queuing of checked vehicles.
11. Every delivery is quantity-checked against the delivery note, with cartons and pallets counted at the dock before further movement.
12. Quality inspection follows unloading immediately, covering visible damage, labelling, batch data and temperature where applicable.
13. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system, so system stock is never created from unchecked deliveries.
14. Compliant goods are system-booked promptly after inspection, creating the basis for onward put-away within the same operational day.
15. Shortages, overages or visible damage identified during counting and inspection are recorded on the delivery record and notified through the defined inbound exception route.
16. Vehicles are released from doors 1-4 only after unloading, inspection recording and booking steps are complete for their load.
17. Harborwick commits to keeping Zone A clear between booked arrivals, so staged inbound freight does not obstruct the next scheduled unloading operation.

title: Dispatch Hours, Capacity and Release
text:
1. Dispatch operates from Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. All packed pallets released from PR-05 Packing and labelling are staged in Zone D only against a confirmed load and door assignment.
2. Standard dispatch hours are Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. No loading, staging or carrier release is committed outside these hours unless overtime has been approved in advance.
3. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Requests for extended dispatch, additional shifts or weekend working are submitted to the warehouse manager with reason, hours, headcount and cost centre before the overtime starts.
4. The building has 8 dock doors, each fitted with a dock leveller. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch exclusively, giving 4 outbound dock doors available for loading in every staffed shift.
5. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, and no trailer or van is staged or loaded without that assignment.
6. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. On that basis we commit a standard outbound capacity of at most 324 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer.
7. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 22000 kg and provide 33 floor pallet positions. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg, so a trailer takes at most 27 full-weight pallets, limited by payload and capped by floor positions.
8. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg and has 6 pallet positions. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; any consignment exceeding that weight or volume is scheduled by trailer.
9. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in the packing-to-dispatch flow. Every outbound pallet presented in Zone D will have been wrapped, labelled, counted and system-released before loading.
10. Release of an outbound load is confirmed only after wrapping, count, door, vehicle and documentation verification. Trailer loads have total kilograms checked against 22000 kg first, then occupied positions checked against 33 before release. The dispatcher releases the load in the system once those checks match, and authorises departure of the trailer or van.

title: Order Accuracy and Packing
text: 1. Harbourwick will maintain Zone C as the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, prepared under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces and picked under PR-04 Order picking. 2. All pick faces will be replenished before the picking shift starts, so that daytime availability supports accurate fulfilment without mid-shift stock-outs. 3. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks, following system-directed locations and quantities for every order line. 4. Under PR-04 Order picking, picked items are scan-verified before packing, and no unverified item will be passed forward to PR-05 Packing and labelling. 5. Harbourwick commits to operate PR-05 Packing and labelling in strict sequence: scan verification, then packing, then labelling, then wrapping without omission. 6. Under this commitment, cartons and totes are packed after successful scan verification, labelled after packing is complete, and then wrapped before transfer onward. 7. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners, and Harbourwick will make sufficient charged units available to sustain scan-verified picking and packing during operating hours. 8. Weighing discipline forms part of accuracy control: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg, and any order exceeding that limit will be built across multiple pallets. 9. Short picks caused by empty faces, damaged stock or unreadable barcodes will be recorded in the scanner task rather than substituted, preserving inventory integrity for replenishment follow-up. 10. Harbourwick will not close a picking task until the system confirms completion of all lines, and will not close a packing task until packing, labelling and wrapping are complete with the correct packed quantity shown. 11. Through replenished faces, scanner-directed picking in Zone C, verification before packing, and ordered packing, labelling and wrapping, Harbourwick provides the order-accuracy standard on which dispatch and invoicing depend. 12. This standard applies to every customer order handled through Zone C on the shared pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners, within the pallet weight limit of 800 kg per pallet including its load. 13. Where a pick face cannot support the ordered quantity, the commitment is to report the exception accurately and preserve the verification sequence, rather than to compromise PR-04 Order picking or PR-05 Packing and labelling controls. 14. Accuracy performance therefore rests on three linked commitments: replenishment before picking starts, scan verification before packing, and packing completed before labelling and wrapping within PR-05 Packing and labelling.

title: Storage Capacity and Put-Away
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides bulk storage in Zone B, the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking, within a warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2.
2. Within that footprint the high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions for booked client stock, available under PR-02 Put-away to storage.
3. Under PR-02 Put-away to storage, no pallet accepted for storage will exceed 800 kg gross weight, including its load.
4. For racked storage, each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg, and loading will respect bay notices at all times.
5. Where free block stacking is agreed outside racking, stacks must not exceed 3 pallets high.
6. In addition to the pallet count limit, free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height under any stacking configuration.
7. To protect access and handling safety, main transport aisles are maintained at 4.0 m wide for powered equipment circulation.
8. Inside the racking blocks, rack storage aisles are maintained at 3.0 m wide to allow compliant reach-truck operation.
9. Inspection precedes record creation: inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system.
10. Only inspected and system-booked stock proceeds to storage, since goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.
11. Consequently put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage will be directed solely from a visible system booking and release entry.
12. During execution operators scan and verify destination, batch and quantity before movement, ensuring booked pallets reach the assigned Zone B location.
13. Ambient reserve pallets released from receiving remain traceable by licence plate from booking through to confirmation in the bulk location.
14. The Provider commits not to exceed the stated rack and stacking limits in order to preserve stock integrity and aisle availability.
15. Clients accept that overweight pallets, overloaded bays or stacks above the agreed height and pallet limits will be held from put-away until made compliant.

title: Counts, Adjustments and Reporting
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. undertakes inventory accuracy for all client stock under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, with controls applied consistently across every storage area and product group. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments, and remain responsible for the integrity of reported balances. Cycle counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule, providing continuous assurance between full stocktakes.

2. Coverage rotates systematically to include bulk, picking, chilled and value-added holdings over successive working days, so all locations are verified on a planned cycle. Every quantity counted during daily activity is recorded with location, quantity and time in the warehouse management system. Results from each daily programme support timely investigation and sustain agreed accuracy levels for client reporting.

3. Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, a second count happens BEFORE any stock adjustment is posted, without exception for urgency or operational pressure.
