Corrections are therefore never applied on the basis of a single count alone, protecting clients against human or scanning error. Discrepancies requiring verification are recounted promptly before any adjustment proposal proceeds to approval.

4. Counting activity is organised within normal operating hours to minimise disruption to inbound, replenishment and dispatch flows. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, providing morning capacity for scheduled cycle counts and recounts. Late coverage runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, allowing continuation of counting, verification and reporting. Handover between shifts preserves count progress, recount status and pending adjustments.

5. A full wall-to-wall stocktake runs once a year, covering every client pallet, carton, pick face and quarantine holding in a single controlled event. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results, confirming that counts, recounts and adjustments have been completed correctly. No stocktake outcome is issued to clients without that formal sign-off.

6. Clients receive a consolidated stocktake report showing counted quantities, verified adjustments and remaining actions for damaged or unreadable labels. Reports distinguish routine cycle-count corrections from annual stocktake adjustments for audit clarity. Agreed accuracy measures are calculated from verified system balances after recounts and authorised adjustments. Performance against those measures is reviewed jointly, with improvement actions documented where thresholds are missed. Queries on reported balances are investigated through recount records and system history.

7. Commitment to daily discipline, recount-before-adjustment and senior sign-off gives clients a stable and auditable inventory service. Throughout the year, stock controllers coordinate counting priorities, recount resources and adjustment governance on behalf of all accounts.

title: Responsibilities and Governance
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides supervised warehouse operations across two staffed shifts each working day.
Coverage comprises Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, followed by Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, with no unsupervised handling between shifts.
2. Accountability for the whole site rests with the warehouse manager for operations, safety and final sign-offs.
Clients receive one accountable owner for service performance, compliance and escalation decisions affecting inventory.
Escalation to the warehouse manager applies where authority is reserved or operational risk requires senior sign-off.
3. During each shift, the shift supervisor runs one shift, directing floor staff and incident response.
Continuity between Shift 1 and Shift 2 is maintained through direct supervisor presence on the floor for the full shift period.
Any incident affecting stock, equipment or service during the shift is owned initially by the duty shift supervisor.
4. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy, including cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
Under this commitment, counting programmes are planned, executed and reconciled by named stock controllers rather than general floor staff.
Recount requirements and adjustment proposals are therefore controlled within the inventory function before senior approval.
5. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads on behalf of clients.
Specifically, the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers in line with inbound and outbound schedules.
Carriers are directed to confirmed doors and slots only, avoiding congestion and unplanned waiting at the dock area.
6. Overtime required to protect inventory accuracy, counts or reporting deadlines is controlled centrally.
Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime, and such approval is obtained before additional hours are worked.
Clients requesting out-of-hours counts or urgent reconciliation will be advised where overtime approval affects timing or cost.
7. Stocktake results are subject to senior sign-off before issue to clients.
Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results, including annual results and supporting recount evidence.
No adjustment or client stock statement becomes final until that sign-off has been recorded in the system.
8. Service integrity includes prompt review of operational incidents affecting inventory or reporting.
The shift supervisor reviews every incident report arising on the shift, ensuring stock impacts are identified and contained.
Where findings require correction to counts, locations or reports, the shift supervisor coordinates with stock controllers and dispatchers.
9. Governance across shift changes is secured through PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
Outgoing supervisors transfer open counts, pending adjustments, dock activity and incident status face to face to incoming supervision.
Clients benefit from uninterrupted ownership of stock accuracy, dock scheduling and escalation from Shift 1 through Shift 2.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. performs PR-09 Damaged-goods handling as the binding process for every damage event covered by this agreement.
2. Every pallet, carton or unit showing crushing, puncture, leakage, contamination, tampering or other visible deterioration is treated as damaged goods from discovery.
3. Inside Zone F, which holds the value-added services area, a dedicated quarantine area provides segregated holding for all such goods.
4. Segregated quarantine status blocks any restock, rework, picking or dispatch until inspection and a documented disposition decision are complete.
5. Promptly after transfer to quarantine, inspection findings, quantities, locations and supporting evidence are recorded in the warehouse system against the client account.
6. Notification describing the affected products, quantities held and preliminary cause is issued to the client without undue delay.
7. Disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling is limited to return to stock, rework, return to supplier or scrap on documented client instruction.
8. Restock, rework or scrap movements are executed only after the disposition has been approved and recorded.
9. Financial write-off authority for damaged goods follows a fixed two-tier threshold agreed for this service.
10. Up to 500 EUR per damage event, the shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs.
11. Above 500 EUR per damage event, the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs.
12. Accordingly, the applicable approval is obtained before any corresponding write-off is posted in the system.
13. Separately, splitting of a single damage event into smaller amounts to use a lower approval tier is not permitted.
14. Clients receive a complete case file for each event, linking the damage report, quarantine location, disposition approval and financial posting.
15. Traceability is preserved from initial discovery through final clearance of the quarantine record.
16. Unresolved quarantine holdings are reviewed regularly and escalated for client direction before any further action.
17. Direct costs of inspection, storage in quarantine, rework or disposal are charged only as agreed in the commercial schedule.
18. Liability for damaged goods remains as set out in the liability provisions of this agreement and is unaffected by the operational handling described here.
19. Jointly, the parties will use damage trends from quarantine records to reduce recurrence and improve packaging and handling controls.

title: Returns Handling
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. accepts customer returns within 14 days of delivery. Requests received after that window will be declined and the goods will not be booked as returns.

2. All authorised returns are processed under PR-07 Returns handling. Harborwick commits to apply that procedure to every return without exception or abbreviated handling.

3. Returned goods are received into Zone F, which holds the value-added services area. No return will be diverted to bulk, picking or dispatch areas before inspection is complete.

4. Harborwick commits that returns are inspected in Zone F. Inspection covers quantity, condition, labelling and packaging integrity, and the result is recorded before any further movement.

5. Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Every inspection produces one of those three proposals, recorded with reasons and supporting evidence.

6. Returns are inspected BEFORE any restock, rework or scrap decision. Harborwick will not restock, rework or scrap any returned unit until inspection and the written proposal are complete.

7. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. No restock, rework or scrap action will proceed without that approval recorded against the return.

8. Approved restock will be returned to saleable inventory through system booking and put-away. Approved rework will be completed and re-inspected before release. Goods approved for scrap will be segregated and disposed of under instruction.

9. Harborwick commits to visibility on every return. The client receives confirmation of receipt in Zone F, the inspection outcome, the proposed restock, rework or scrap route, and the shift supervisor approval with date and time.

10. Returns that cannot be immediately dispositioned remain under control in Zone F pending approval. Harborwick will not release quarantined or disputed returns to stock, dispatch or general storage.

11. Harborwick staffs and equips Zone F to meet the 14-day commitment. Returns staff are assigned to inspect returns in Zone F each working day, and the shift supervisor reviews pending dispositions to prevent backlog.

12. Performance against this commitment is reported per return and in aggregate. Harborwick reports volumes received, inspection turnaround, disposition split between restock, rework or scrap, and approval compliance under PR-07 Returns handling.

title: Chilled Storage Service
text:
1. Harborwick provides chilled storage for suitable client products in Zone E under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
Allocation within Zone E follows product compatibility and available capacity at time of booking.

2. We maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C throughout storage and handling.
Continuous monitoring supports prompt detection of any downward drift toward the lower limit.
Doors, curtains and traffic flows are managed to protect temperature stability during put-away and access.
Chilled consignments receive priority movement to minimise exposure outside the controlled environment.

3. We maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C throughout storage and handling.
Cooling performance is monitored to prevent any upward excursion above the upper limit.
Access to Zone E is controlled to avoid unnecessary heat ingress during normal operations.
Suspect stock affected by any excursion is segregated pending instruction.

4. All chilled inbound is handled under PR-02 Put-away to storage in combination with PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.
Booking confirms product identity, quantity and temperature requirement before any movement to Zone E.
Only released chilled products are directed to Zone E after booking is complete.

5. Cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
Verification is recorded with reading, time and responsible person for audit purposes.
Readings confirm that conditions remain within +2 to +8 °C at the point of check.
Trends approaching either limit trigger preventive action before a breach occurs.

6. Any deviation outside +2 to +8 °C is escalated under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
Affected pallets remain in Zone E under hold status until assessed.
Clients receive notification of the deviation, quantity involved and corrective action taken.
No suspect chilled stock is picked, packed or dispatched without documented clearance.

7. Replenishment, picking and dispatch of chilled lines preserve the cold chain wherever operationally possible.
Dwell time outside Zone E is kept to the minimum needed for each task.
Staging of chilled pallets uses the designated controlled area before loading.
Documentation for outbound chilled loads records handling in line with PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

8. Reporting on chilled storage forms part of the routine inventory service.
Temperature verification records for Zone E are retained and available to the client on request.
Monthly summaries confirm compliance with the +2 to +8 °C commitment and any incidents.
Service reviews address capacity needs, seasonal volumes and handling improvements for chilled products.
